children.title: Polynomial-Spectral Acceleration Family
children.top_down_role: Polynomial filtering of affine or locally linear fixed-point dynamics.

children.title: Chebyshev Semi-Iteration
children.top_down_role: Polynomial acceleration based on spectral localization.

children.title: Known Spectral-Window Regime
children.top_down_role: Chebyshev acceleration with usable spectral bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Known Spectral-Window Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chebyshev semi-iteration for a symmetric positive-definite linear system with known spectral endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\) be symmetric positive definite with known \(0<\mu\leq\lambda_{\min}(A)\leq\lambda_{\max}(A)\leq L\), and solve \(Ax=b\) using degree-\(m\) Chebyshev semi-iteration. Its error has the form \(e_m=p_m(A)e_0\), where \(p_m(0)=1\) and \(p_m\) is the scaled Chebyshev minimax polynomial on \([\mu,L]\). With \(\kappa=L/\mu\),
\[\lVert e_m\rVert_A\leq2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^m\lVert e_0\rVert_A.\]
Thus \(m=O(\sqrt\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon))\) matrix-vector products suffice for relative \(A\)-norm error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Known spectral endpoints permit a Chebyshev minimax schedule, achieving relative energy-norm error epsilon in order square-root condition number times log inverse epsilon matrix-vector products.
assumptions_latex: Each semi-iteration uses one multiplication by \(A\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the leaf and the Chebyshev estimate is standard for the stated SPD setting, but the exact constant, norm bound, and matrix-vector-product convention lack an authoritative locator.

children.title: Adaptive Spectral Localization
children.top_down_role: Policies that estimate spectral information during iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Spectral Localization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded Chebyshev restarts using spectral bounds estimated from observed Krylov information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\) with symmetric positive-definite \(A\), choose \(x_0\), initial safeguards \(0<\underline\mu_0\leq\overline L_0\), a block length \(q\geq1\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). During each block, collect residuals and matrix-vector products, form a symmetric projected matrix \(H_k=V_k^TAV_k\) on the available orthonormal Krylov basis, and compute Ritz extremes \(\theta_{\min}(H_k)\), \(\theta_{\max}(H_k)\). Select safeguarded bounds \(0<\underline\mu_k\leq	heta_{\min}(H_k)\) and \(\overline L_k\geq	heta_{\max}(H_k)\), then run the next Chebyshev block using \([\underline\mu_k,\overline L_k]\). Stop when \(\lVert b-Ax_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\). Ritz containment alone does not certify enclosure of the unobserved spectrum, so external safety margins or validated bounds are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive localization estimates spectral extremes from Krylov projections and restarts Chebyshev blocks with safeguarded intervals. Ritz values alone do not certify the entire spectrum.
assumptions_latex: An orthonormal Krylov basis can be formed from observed products
Chosen spectral intervals are positive and safeguarded
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each restarted block uses observed spectral estimates, but global Chebyshev guarantees require certified enclosures of \(\sigma(A)\).

notation.meaning: Projected symmetric matrix on the observed Krylov subspace.
Safeguarded spectral interval used by a Chebyshev block.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm correctly warns that Ritz extremes do not certify enclosure of the unobserved spectrum, but the restart and safeguarding policy is not uniquely specified and has no authoritative source.

children.title: Spectral Misspecification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of stability or acceleration under inaccurate spectral localization.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Misspecification Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chebyshev semi-iteration for a self-adjoint linear fixed-point error map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the error iteration be \(e_{j+1}=Ge_j\), where \(G\) is self-adjoint and the degree-\(k\) Chebyshev polynomial \(p_k\) is designed using a presumed interval \([a,b]\subset(-1,1)\), with \(p_k(1)=1\). The accelerated error is \(e_k^{\mathrm{acc}}=p_k(G)e_0\), hence \(\|e_k^{\mathrm{acc}}\|\leq \max_{\lambda\in\sigma(G)}|p_k(\lambda)|\,\|e_0\|\). The advertised Chebyshev contraction is valid only when \(\sigma(G)\subseteq[a,b]\). If the true spectrum contains \(\lambda_\star\notin[a,b]\), acceleration is lost whenever \(|p_k(\lambda_\star)|\) exceeds the unaccelerated factor, and stability fails whenever \(|p_k(\lambda_\star)|>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Chebyshev schedule is guaranteed only on its design interval; an eigenvalue outside that interval can erase acceleration or amplify its eigencomponent beyond one.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a bounded self-adjoint linear operator.
\([a,b]\subset(-1,1)\) is the spectral interval used to design \(p_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma(G)\nsubseteq[a,b]\) removes the designed uniform bound, and \(|p_k(\lambda_\star)|>1\) yields amplification along the corresponding spectral component.

children.title: Minimal-Residual Polynomial Families
children.top_down_role: Residual-minimizing polynomial accelerators related to Krylov methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Residual Polynomial Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial residual minimization for a nonsingular finite-dimensional linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), choose \(x_0\) with residual \(r_0=b-Ax_0\). At degree \(k\), a minimal-residual polynomial method selects \(q_k\in\mathcal P_k\) satisfying \(q_k(0)=1\) and \(\|q_k(A)r_0\|=\min_{q\in\mathcal P_k,\,q(0)=1}\|q(A)r_0\|\). Equivalently, it chooses \(x_k\in x_0+\mathcal K_k(A,r_0)\) minimizing \(\|b-Ax_k\|\), where \(\mathcal K_k(A,r_0)=\operatorname{span}\{r_0,Ar_0,\ldots,A^{k-1}r_0\}\). Thus \(r_k=q_k(A)r_0\), and termination occurs by the grade of \(r_0\) when arithmetic is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimal-residual polynomial methods choose the Krylov-space iterate whose residual norm is smallest, equivalently applying an optimal normalized polynomial to the initial residual.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a nonsingular linear operator on a finite-dimensional normed space.
The residual norm and polynomial degree are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_k=q_k(A)r_0\) has minimum norm among residuals attainable from \(x_0+\mathcal K_k(A,r_0)\).

notation.meaning: Polynomials of degree at most k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial and Krylov formulations are plausible, but the residual norm, equivalence, and exact-arithmetic termination-by-grade assertion require an authoritative Krylov-method source with a precise locator.

children.title: Vector Extrapolation
children.top_down_role: Vector sequence transformations based on polynomial, rank, or epsilon constructions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iteration threshold for absolute objective accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conditional conversion of the stated relative-scale error estimate into an additive epsilon guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L,R,\epsilon>0\), \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), and \(\delta(\epsilon):=\epsilon/(\epsilon+2LR)\in(0,1)\). Suppose that for some \(k\in\mathbb{N}\), an iterate \(x_k^*\) satisfies
\[
\phi(x_k^*)-\phi^*\le LR\left[\frac{\delta}{1-\delta}+\frac{1}{2n\bigl(e^{\delta(k+1)/n}-1\bigr)(1-\delta)}\right],\qquad \delta=\delta(\epsilon).
\]
If
\[
k\ge T_n(\epsilon):=\frac{n}{\delta(\epsilon)}\ln\!\left(1+\frac{LR}{n\epsilon(1-\delta(\epsilon))}\right)=n\left(1+2\frac{LR}{\epsilon}\right)\ln\!\left(1+\frac{\epsilon+2LR}{2n\epsilon}\right),
\]
then \(\phi(x_k^*)\le\phi^*+\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive L, R, and epsilon and a positive integer dimension n, set delta to epsilon divided by epsilon plus 2LR. If the kth iterate obeys the stated relative-scale error estimate and k is at least the displayed threshold T_n(epsilon), then its objective value is within epsilon of the optimum.

children.title: Minimal Polynomial Extrapolation
children.top_down_role: The minimal-polynomial branch of vector extrapolation.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Polynomial Extrapolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical MPE applied to consecutive vectors in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0,\ldots,x_{k+1}\), form \(u_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\). Determine \(c_0,\ldots,c_{k-1}\) from \(\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}c_i u_i=-u_k\), set \(c_k=1\), and require \(s=\sum_{i=0}^k c_i\neq0\). Define \(\gamma_i=c_i/s\) and output \(y_k=\sum_{i=0}^k\gamma_i x_i\). If the linear system is inconsistent, its least-squares solution defines the usual numerical variant. For a linearly generated sequence whose error satisfies a minimal-polynomial relation of degree at most \(k\), exact arithmetic gives the limit whenever the normalization denominator is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MPE fits a linear dependence among consecutive differences, normalizes its coefficients to sum to one, and forms the corresponding affine combination of iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(x_0,\ldots,x_{k+1}\) lie in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.

notation.meaning: Coefficients of the fitted difference relation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The MPE construction and its exactness claim require a vector-extrapolation source because indexing and least-squares conventions vary. The plain statement also omits the exactness assertion contained in the LaTeX statement.

children.title: Reduced Rank Extrapolation
children.top_down_role: The reduced-rank branch of vector extrapolation.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Rank Extrapolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical RRE as constrained residual minimization over consecutive differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0,\ldots,x_{k+1}\) in a finite-dimensional inner-product space, set \(u_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\) for \(0\leq i\leq k\). Compute \(\gamma\in\mathbb R^{k+1}\) by solving \(\min_{\gamma}\|\sum_{i=0}^k\gamma_i u_i\|\) subject to \(\sum_{i=0}^k\gamma_i=1\), and output \(y_k=\sum_{i=0}^k\gamma_i x_i\). When the Gram matrix \(U^{\mathsf T}U\) is nonsingular, \(\gamma=(U^{\mathsf T}U)^{-1}\mathbf1/[\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}(U^{\mathsf T}U)^{-1}\mathbf1]\), where \(U=[u_0\ \cdots\ u_k]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: RRE forms the affine combination of iterates whose same coefficients produce the smallest norm combination of their consecutive differences.
assumptions_latex: The vectors lie in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
The affine constraint is feasible; the closed formula additionally requires \(U^{\mathsf T}U\) nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k=\sum_{i=0}^k\gamma_i x_i\) minimizes the difference-based residual surrogate under \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\gamma=1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constrained least-squares formulation is plausible for classical RRE, but its indexing and closed coefficient formula require an authoritative vector-extrapolation citation.

children.title: Epsilon Transformation Family
children.top_down_role: Vector and topological extensions of epsilon transformations.

children.title: Vector Epsilon Families
children.top_down_role: Vector-valued extensions of epsilon transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Vector Epsilon Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wynn-type vector epsilon recursion using the Euclidean vector inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sequence \((x_n)\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), initialize \(\varepsilon_{-1}^{(n)}=0\) and \(\varepsilon_0^{(n)}=x_n\). Define the Euclidean vector inverse by \(v^{-1}=v/\|v\|_2^2\) for \(v\neq0\), and recursively compute \(\varepsilon_{j+1}^{(n)}=\varepsilon_{j-1}^{(n+1)}+(\varepsilon_j^{(n+1)}-\varepsilon_j^{(n)})^{-1}\). The accelerated estimates are the even entries \(\varepsilon_{2m}^{(n)}\). A table entry is undefined when its difference denominator is zero; practical variants stop, restart, or regularize when that denominator is numerically small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The vector epsilon algorithm extends Wynn’s table by replacing scalar reciprocals with normalized vector inverses; even table entries are extrapolated estimates.
assumptions_latex: Every inverted table difference is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family returns \(\varepsilon_{2m}^{(n)}\) as its order-m accelerated estimate.

notation.meaning: Entry of the vector epsilon table.
Euclidean vector inverse v divided by its squared norm.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Several vector epsilon algorithms use different vector inverses or auxiliary constructions. A specific source is required to establish that this recursion and its even-entry interpretation match the intended family.

children.title: Topological Epsilon Families
children.top_down_role: Topological extensions using problem-adapted dual or scalarizing structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Topological Epsilon Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First topological epsilon algorithm on a vector space paired with its dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, fix nonzero \(y\in X^*\), and initialize \(\varepsilon_{-1}^{(n)}=0\in X^*\), \(\varepsilon_0^{(n)}=x_n\in X\). Alternately define \(\varepsilon_{2k+1}^{(n)}=\varepsilon_{2k-1}^{(n+1)}+y/\langle y,\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n+1)}-\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}\rangle\) and \(\varepsilon_{2k+2}^{(n)}=\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n+1)}+[\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n+1)}-\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}]/\langle\varepsilon_{2k+1}^{(n+1)}-\varepsilon_{2k+1}^{(n)},\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n+1)}-\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}\rangle\). Even entries are vector extrapolates, provided every displayed denominator is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Topological epsilon alternates primal and dual table entries, using a fixed functional to replace the unavailable reciprocal of a vector.
assumptions_latex: All scalar pairings used as denominators are nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}\in X\) is the order-k topological epsilon extrapolate.

notation.meaning: Dual pairing of f and x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed primal-dual recursion appears consistent with a first topological epsilon variant, but this specialized formula must be checked against a source identifying the exact variant and indexing convention.

children.title: Epsilon-Family Correspondences
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships among scalar, vector, and topological epsilon variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-Family Correspondences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection correspondence between the first topological and scalar epsilon algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_n)\subset X\), fix \(y\in X^*\), and set \(s_n=\langle y,x_n\rangle\). Construct the first topological epsilon table from \((x_n)\) using \(y\), and construct Wynn's scalar epsilon table \((e_j^{(n)})\) from \((s_n)\), with identical initial indexing. Whenever both recursions are defined, their even entries satisfy \(\langle y,\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}\rangle=e_{2k}^{(n)}\). Thus applying the functional after topological extrapolation reproduces scalar epsilon extrapolation of the projected sequence, although the vector \(\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}\) contains information not determined by that scalar identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a topological epsilon extrapolate by its defining functional gives the scalar epsilon extrapolate of the projected input sequence.
assumptions_latex: The scalar and topological epsilon tables use matching indexing.
Every denominator required by both recursions is nonzero.

notation.meaning: Scalar projection of x_n by y.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection identity depends on the precise topological epsilon recursion and matching scalar-table convention. A source explicitly stating this correspondence is required.

children.title: Numerical-Rank Extrapolation Family
children.top_down_role: Rank-aware numerical variants for dependent iterate histories.

children.title: Rank-Revealing Extrapolation
children.top_down_role: Extrapolation variants that expose dependent or nearly dependent history.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing Extrapolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient stabilization by rank-revealing factorization of a difference matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given iterates \(x_0,\ldots,x_{k+1}\), form \(U=[x_1-x_0\ \cdots\ x_{k+1}-x_k]\). Compute a column-pivoted QR factorization \(U\Pi=QR\), select \(r\) from a prescribed rank test on the diagonal or trailing blocks of \(R\), and retain the corresponding independent columns in \(U_r\). Solve the chosen extrapolation coefficient problem on \(U_r\), enforcing that its affine coefficients sum to one, then output the associated affine combination of iterates. The factorization exposes dependent directions before coefficient formation and prevents inversion of the discarded rank-deficient block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-revealing extrapolation detects dependent trajectory differences before solving for affine extrapolation coefficients and discards directions that fail a specified rank test.
assumptions_latex: The extrapolation method is expressed through a matrix of consecutive differences.
A numerical-rank tolerance and coefficient rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficient solve is restricted to an estimated rank-\(r\) subspace rather than the full ill-conditioned difference matrix.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives a generic rank-revealing template rather than a fixed extrapolation algorithm: the rank test, coefficient problem, and mapping from pivoted difference columns to affine iterate coefficients remain unspecified. A source defining the intended family is required.

children.title: SVD-Based Extrapolation
children.top_down_role: Extrapolation variants using singular-value decompositions.

knowledge_statements.title: SVD-Based Extrapolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated-SVD stabilization of difference-based vector extrapolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form the difference matrix \(U=[x_1-x_0\ \cdots\ x_{k+1}-x_k]\) and compute \(U=P\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\). For a threshold \(\tau>0\), retain indices \(I_\tau=\{i:\sigma_i>\tau\}\) and define \(U_\tau^+=V_{I_\tau}\Sigma_{I_\tau}^{-1}P_{I_\tau}^{\mathsf T}\). Replace every inverse or least-squares solve involving \(U\) by the truncated pseudoinverse \(U_\tau^+\), impose the extrapolation method's affine normalization, and output the resulting affine combination of stored iterates. Components associated with singular values at most \(\tau\) contribute zero to the coefficient solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SVD-based extrapolation computes coefficients only from well-resolved singular directions of the trajectory-difference matrix, suppressing unstable inverse factors.
assumptions_latex: The iterates lie in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stabilized solve uses \(U_\tau^+\), whose operator norm is at most \(1/\min_{i\in I_\tau}\sigma_i\) when \(I_\tau\neq\varnothing\).

children.title: Numerical-Rank Truncation
children.top_down_role: History reduction governed by detected numerical rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Rank Truncation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative singular-value rule for retaining extrapolation directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb R^{d\times m}\) have singular values \(\sigma_1\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_q\geq0\), where \(q=\min\{d,m\}\). Given relative tolerance \(\eta\in(0,1)\) and absolute tolerance \(\delta\geq0\), define \(\tau=\max\{\delta,\eta\sigma_1\}\) and numerical rank \(r=\#\{i:\sigma_i>\tau\}\). Numerical-rank extrapolation retains the first \(r\) singular directions and discards the remainder. The retained inverse factors satisfy \(\sigma_i^{-1}<\tau^{-1}\) when \(\tau>0\), while directions indistinguishable from zero at the prescribed resolution are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical rank is the number of singular values above combined absolute and relative tolerances; only those directions enter the extrapolation solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r=\#\{i:\sigma_i>\max(\delta,\eta\sigma_1)\}\), and directions indexed above \(r\) are discarded.

children.title: Trajectory-Separated Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Accelerated estimates kept separate from the base trajectory.

children.title: Offline Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Acceleration performed after collecting a base trajectory.

knowledge_statements.title: Offline Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceleration computed after an unmodified fixed-point trajectory has been generated in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and \(T:X\to X\). First generate and store \(x_{i+1}=T(x_i)\) for \(0\leq i<m\), without feeding extrapolated points into this recursion. Afterward choose \(c\in\mathbb R^{m+1}\) by a specified regularized residual or difference criterion subject to \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}c=1\), and output \(y=\sum_{i=0}^m c_i x_i\). For example, with the residual operator \(R:\mathbb R^{m+1}\to X\) defined by \(Rc=\sum_{i=0}^m c_i(T(x_i)-x_i)\), one may solve \(\min_{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}c=1}\|Rc\|^2+\lambda\|c\|_2^2\), where \(\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Offline acceleration first generates the unmodified base trajectory and then computes a regularized affine combination of stored iterates without feeding that estimate back into the iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and \(T:X\to X\).
The stored iterates \(x_0,\ldots,x_m\), coefficient criterion, and regularization parameter are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(y\) depends only on stored trajectory data and does not alter any base iterate \(x_i\).

notation.meaning: Linear residual operator formed from the stored fixed-point residuals.

children.title: Postprocessing-Only Estimates
children.top_down_role: Accelerated estimates retained outside the evolving base iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Postprocessing-Only Estimates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of reported extrapolates from the state sequence used by the base method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the base trajectory satisfy \(x_{n+1}=T_n(x_n)\). At selected indices, let a postprocessor produce \(y_n=\Phi_n(x_0,\ldots,x_n)\), but require the next state to remain \(x_{n+1}=T_n(x_n)\), independently of \(y_n\). Then the complete base sequence is identical to the sequence obtained without postprocessing. Consequently, every convergence or stability guarantee proved solely for the maps \(T_n\) and the initial state remains applicable to \((x_n)\); any claim about improved accuracy of \((y_n)\) requires a separate estimate and cannot be inferred from base-trajectory convergence alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A postprocessing estimate never becomes an iteration state, so it cannot disturb the base trajectory; its improved accuracy nevertheless needs an independent guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Each base update uses only the prescribed state and map \(T_n\).
The reported estimate \(y_n\) is not fed into any later base update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Postprocessing leaves \((x_n)\) unchanged, while guarantees for \((y_n)\) must be established separately.

notation.meaning: Base iteration map at step n.

children.title: Base-Trajectory Separation
children.top_down_role: Interfaces that preserve the original trajectory while producing accelerated outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Base-Trajectory Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Offline nonlinear acceleration that leaves the generating fixed-point trajectory unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\), and choose \(x_0\in H\). Generate the base trajectory independently by \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\). For selected indices \(0\le i_0<\cdots<i_m\le k\), compute coefficients \(c^{(k)}\in\mathbb{R}^{m+1}\) from the stored iterates or residuals, subject to \(\sum_{j=0}^{m}c_j^{(k)}=1\), and form \(y_k=\sum_{j=0}^{m}c_j^{(k)}x_{i_j}\). Base-trajectory separation requires that every subsequent base iterate remain \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\), independently of \(y_k\). Thus \(y_k\) is an accelerated estimate or postprocessed output and is never used as an input to \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate Picard iterates unchanged, then form affine accelerated estimates from stored iterates without feeding those estimates back into the base process.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\) is evaluable.
The coefficient rule returns finite affine coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k\) does not affect any base update \(x_{j+1}=T(x_j)\).

children.title: Feedback-Reinjected Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Accelerated estimates returned to the evolving trajectory.

children.title: Online Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Acceleration computed during the evolving fixed-point process.

knowledge_statements.title: Online Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential acceleration whose current estimate is computed and used before the next operator evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\), choose \(x_0\in H\), and fix a memory bound \(m\ge 0\). At iteration \(k\), set \(I_k=\{\max(0,k-m),\ldots,k\}\), compute coefficients \(c^{(k)}=(c_i^{(k)})_{i\in I_k}\) from information available through iteration \(k\), and require \(\sum_{i\in I_k}c_i^{(k)}=1\). Form the online extrapolate \(y_k=\sum_{i\in I_k}c_i^{(k)}x_i\), evaluate \(x_{k+1}=T(y_k)\), and then append the new iterate and residual to the history. Stop when a prescribed residual test such as \(\|T(y_k)-y_k\|\le\varepsilon\) holds; otherwise output the latest \(y_k\) or \(x_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, compute an affine estimate from currently available history and immediately use it for the next fixed-point evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\) is evaluable.
The coefficient rule uses no information from iterations later than \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=T\!\left(\sum_{i\in I_k}c_i^{(k)}x_i\right)\) is an online, feedback-reinjected update.

notation.meaning: Available finite-memory history at iteration k.

children.title: Reinjected Acceleration

knowledge_statements.title: Reinjected Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine extrapolation fed back as the input of the next fixed-point evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:H\to H\), choose \(x_0\in H\), and retain a finite index set \(I_k\subseteq\{0,
obreak\ldots,
obreak k\}\). Given stored iterates, choose coefficients \(c_i^{(k)}\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in I_k}c_i^{(k)}=1\), form \(y_k=\sum_{i\in I_k}c_i^{(k)}x_i\), and reinject this estimate through \(x_{k+1}=T(y_k)\). The next coefficient vector may depend on the augmented history containing \(x_{k+1}\). If the residual satisfies \(\|x_{k+1}-y_k\|\le\varepsilon\), return \(y_k\); otherwise repeat. Unlike trajectory-separated postprocessing, the generated sequence generally differs from the Picard trajectory \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build an affine extrapolate from past iterates and feed it into the operator, thereby changing all later iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\) is evaluable.
Each coefficient vector is finite and affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accelerated estimate is reinjected by \(x_{k+1}=T(y_k)\), so it influences the future trajectory.

notation.meaning: Affine extrapolate supplied to the operator.

children.title: Feedback Stability
children.top_down_role: Stability considerations created by reinjecting accelerated estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Feedback Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform Lyapunov contraction condition for a finite-memory reinjected acceleration loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge1\), let \(Z=H^m\), and let \(\Phi_k:Z\to Z\) be the closed-loop state map induced by an online accelerator followed by operator evaluation, so the history state obeys \(z_{k+1}=\Phi_k(z_k)\). For a fixed point \(x_\star=T(x_\star)\), write \(z_\star=(x_\star,\ldots,x_\star)\). The feedback loop is uniformly stable if there exist a positive-definite self-adjoint operator \(P:Z\to Z\) and \(\rho\in[0,1)\) such that, for every admissible \(k\) and \(z\in Z\), \(\|\Phi_k(z)-z_\star\|_P\le\rho\|z-z_\star\|_P\), where \(\|z\|_P^2=\langle Pz,z\rangle\). Consequently, \(\|z_k-z_\star\|_P\le\rho^k\|z_0-z_\star\|_P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feedback stability holds when every closed-loop history update contracts a common Lyapunov norm uniformly, implying geometric convergence to the fixed history.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and the accelerator has memory \(m\).
The constant history \(z_\star\) is invariant under every \(\Phi_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|z_k-z_\star\|_P\le\rho^k\|z_0-z_\star\|_P\), hence the reinjected loop is geometrically stable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The common-Lyapunov contraction condition is mathematically coherent and sufficient for the displayed estimate, but no citation supports this particular closed-loop state model or its use as the local feedback-stability notion.

children.title: Deterministic Perturbation Stability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity to nonlinear modeling error and inexact base iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Perturbation Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise sensitivity bounds for contractive base iterations and affine extrapolation with bounded coefficient gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be a \(q\)-contraction with \(0\le q<1\). Suppose \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\) and \(\widetilde x_{k+1}=T(\widetilde x_k)+d_k\), where \(\|d_k\|\le\varepsilon_k\). Then \(\|\widetilde x_k-x_k\|\le q^k\|\widetilde x_0-x_0\|+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-j}\varepsilon_j\). Moreover, for a common affine coefficient vector satisfying \(\sum_{i\in I}c_i=1\) and \(\|c\|_1\le C\), the extrapolates \(y=\sum_{i\in I}c_ix_i\) and \(\widetilde y=\sum_{i\in I}c_i\widetilde x_i\) obey \(\|\widetilde y-y\|\le C\max_{i\in I}\|\widetilde x_i-x_i\|\). Thus regularization controlling \(\|c\|_1\) limits deterministic error amplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contractive iteration filters deterministic errors geometrically, while affine extrapolation amplifies stored-iterate errors by at most the coefficient one-norm.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a normed space and \(T\) is a \(q\)-contraction.
The same affine coefficients are applied to both histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widetilde y-y\|\le C\max_{i\in I}\|\widetilde x_i-x_i\|\), with base errors bounded by the displayed geometric convolution.

notation.meaning: Deterministic error in the kth operator evaluation.
Contraction modulus of the base operator.
Upper bound on the extrapolation coefficient one-norm.

children.title: Stochastic Extrapolation Stability
children.top_down_role: Noise-aware extrapolation and variance-dominated limitations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Extrapolation Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional second-moment law and equal-variance noise floor for affine extrapolation of noisy fixed-point iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(I\) be a finite index set, and let \(\widehat x_i=x_i+\xi_i\in H\) for \(i\in I\). Conditional on a sigma-algebra \(\mathcal F\), assume that the errors \((\xi_i)_{i\in I}\) are independent, satisfy \(\mathbb E[\xi_i\mid\mathcal F]=0\), and are square-integrable. Let the coefficients \((c_i)_{i\in I}\) and base iterates \((x_i)_{i\in I}\) be \(\mathcal F\)-measurable, with \(\sum_{i\in I}c_i=1\), and define \(y=\sum_{i\in I}c_ix_i\) and \(\widehat y=\sum_{i\in I}c_i\widehat x_i\). Then \(\mathbb E[\widehat y-y\mid\mathcal F]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\|\widehat y-y\|^2\mid\mathcal F]=\sum_{i\in I}c_i^2\mathbb E[\|\xi_i\|^2\mid\mathcal F]\). Consequently, if \(\mathbb E[\|\xi_i\|^2\mid\mathcal F]\le\sigma_i^2\), then \(\mathbb E[\|\widehat y-y\|^2\mid\mathcal F]\le\sum_{i\in I}c_i^2\sigma_i^2\). If instead \(\mathbb E[\|\xi_i\|^2\mid\mathcal F]=\sigma^2\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(|I|=m\ge1\), then \(\mathbb E[\|\widehat y-y\|^2\mid\mathcal F]=\sigma^2\sum_{i\in I}c_i^2\ge\sigma^2/m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditionally independent centered iterate errors contribute according to the squared affine coefficients. Second-moment upper bounds give an upper estimate, while exact equal conditional second moments yield a noise floor of sigma squared divided by the history size.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(I\) is finite.
The coefficients and base iterates are \(\mathcal F\)-measurable.
Conditional errors are independent, centered, and square-integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\|\widehat y-y\|^2\mid\mathcal F]=\sum_{i\in I}c_i^2\mathbb E[\|\xi_i\|^2\mid\mathcal F]\); under exact equal conditional second moments \(\sigma^2\), this quantity is at least \(\sigma^2/m\).

notation.meaning: Noise in the ith stored iterate.

children.title: Inertial Picard Families

knowledge_statements.title: Inertial Picard Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-step Picard iteration evaluated at an inertially extrapolated point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty subset of a real Hilbert space \(H\), let \(T:C\to C\), and choose \(x_{-1},x_0\in C\). For prescribed inertial parameters \((\beta_k)_{k\ge0}\), form \(y_k=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\) and require \(y_k\in C\). The inertial Picard update is \(x_{k+1}=T(y_k)\). Continue until a selected fixed-point residual, such as \(\|T(y_k)-y_k\|\), is at most \(\varepsilon\), and return \(y_k\) or \(x_{k+1}\). knowledge_statements.title: Inertial Mann Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxed fixed-point iteration evaluated after a two-step inertial extrapolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty convex subset of a real Hilbert space \(H\), let \(T:C\to C\), and choose \(x_{-1},x_0\in C\). Given inertial parameters \(\beta_k\) and relaxation parameters \(\lambda_k\in(0,1]\), compute \(y_k=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\), require \(y_k\in C\), and update \(x_{k+1}=(1-\lambda_k)y_k+\lambda_kT(y_k)\). Stop when \(\|T(y_k)-y_k\|\le\varepsilon\), and return \(y_k\) or \(x_{k+1}\). Setting \(\beta_k=0\) gives a Mann iteration, while additionally setting \(\lambda_k=1\) gives ordinary Picard iteration; convergence needs operator-dependent bounds on both parameter sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a relaxed fixed-point step at an inertially extrapolated point; removing inertia yields Mann iteration, and full relaxation yields Picard iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty and convex, and \(T:C\to C\).

children.title: Direct–Averaged Inertial Transfer
children.top_down_role: Structural transfer of inertial mechanisms between direct and averaged baselines.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct–Averaged Inertial Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic equivalence between constant-relaxation inertial Mann iteration and inertial Picard iteration for the relaxed operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a convex subset of a real normed space, let \(T:C\to C\), and let \(\lambda\in(0,1]\). Define the relaxed operator \(T_\lambda=(1-\lambda)I+\lambda T\). For any inertial sequence \((\beta_k)\), set \(y_k=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\) and assume \(y_k\in C\). Then the constant-relaxation inertial Mann update \(x_{k+1}=(1-\lambda)y_k+\lambda T(y_k)\) is exactly the inertial Picard update \(x_{k+1}=T_\lambda(y_k)\), and \(\operatorname{Fix}(T_\lambda)=\operatorname{Fix}(T)\). If the ambient space is a Hilbert space, \(T\) is nonexpansive, and \(\lambda\in(0,1)\), then \(T_\lambda\) is \(\lambda\)-averaged. Results for inertial direct iteration of \(T_\lambda\) therefore transfer to the constant-relaxation inertial Mann scheme subject to their original hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constant-relaxation inertial Mann iteration is inertial Picard iteration applied to the corresponding relaxed operator, and the two operators have the same fixed points. Under nonexpansiveness and a relaxation strictly between zero and one, the relaxed operator is averaged.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation is constant and satisfies \(0<\lambda\le1\).

notation.meaning: Relaxed operator, which is lambda-averaged when T is nonexpansive and lambda lies strictly between zero and one.

knowledge_statements.title: Inertial Proximal Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal point iteration applied at a two-step inertially extrapolated argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone, choose \(x_{-1},x_0\in H\), and select \(\gamma_k>0\) and inertial parameters \(\beta_k\). Compute \(y_k=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\) and \(x_{k+1}=J_{\gamma_k A}(y_k)=(I+\gamma_kA)^{-1}(y_k)\). Equivalently, the update is certified by \((y_k-x_{k+1})/\gamma_k\in A(x_{k+1})\). Stop when \(\|y_k-x_{k+1}\|/\gamma_k\le\varepsilon\), and return \(x_{k+1}\). The choice \(\beta_k=0\) recovers the proximal point method; convergence of the inertial family requires additional restrictions on \((\beta_k)\) and \((\gamma_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extrapolate using the last displacement, then apply the resolvent of a maximally monotone operator; zero inertia recovers proximal point iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A\) is maximally monotone.

knowledge_statements.title: Inertial Splitting Families

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(S:H\to H\) be a fixed-point operator obtained from a monotone-operator splitting scheme, with solutions recovered from \(\operatorname{Fix}(S)\). Stop when \(\|S(y_k)-y_k\|\le\varepsilon\), and output the solution represented by \(y_k\) or \(x_{k+1}\). This template covers inertial versions of forward-backward and other fixed-point splittings once their specific operator \(S\), stepsize conditions, and solution-recovery map are supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Wrap a splitting fixed-point map in two-step inertial extrapolation, retaining the original map's fixed-point encoding of solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(S:H\to H\) is a well-defined splitting fixed-point map.
The chosen splitting supplies a valid recovery map from \(\operatorname{Fix}(S)\) to solutions.

children.title: Resolvent-to-Splitting Transfer
children.top_down_role: Connections between inertial resolvent constructions and splitting realizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent-to-Splitting Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-backward splitting represented as resolvent evaluation at a forward step, with inertia transferred unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone, and let \(B:H\to H\) be single-valued. For \(\gamma>0\), define the forward-backward map \(S_\gamma=J_{\gamma A}\circ(I-\gamma B)\). Then \(x\in\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\) if and only if \(x\in\operatorname{Fix}(S_\gamma)\). Consequently, applying inertial Picard iteration to \(S_\gamma\) gives \(y_k=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\) and \(x_{k+1}=J_{\gamma A}(y_k-\gamma B(y_k))\). Thus the inertial resolvent template transfers to forward-backward splitting by replacing the resolvent input \(y_k\) with the forward-corrected input \(y_k-\gamma B(y_k)\); convergence additionally requires the usual regularity and stepsize conditions on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zeros of a sum are fixed points of the forward-backward map, so inertial resolvent iteration transfers by adding a forward correction.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A\) is maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{zer}(A+B)=\operatorname{Fix}\!\left(J_{\gamma A}(I-\gamma B)\right)\), yielding the displayed inertial splitting update.

notation.meaning: Solution set of the monotone inclusion.

children.title: Inertial Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Oscillation, energy growth, and parameter sensitivity in inertial schemes.

knowledge_statements.title: Inertial Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Schur-stability boundary for a real scalar mode of a stationary inertial fixed-point iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q,\beta\in\mathbb{R}\) and consider \(x_{k+1}=q x_k+\beta(x_k-x_{k-1})\). Its characteristic polynomial is \(p(\lambda)=\lambda^2-(q+\beta)\lambda+\beta\). Every trajectory converges to zero for all initial pairs \((x_{-1},x_0)\) if and only if
\[|\beta|<1,\qquad q<1,\qquad 1+q+2\beta>0.\]
Equality in any nonredundant boundary condition permits a characteristic root on the unit circle; violation places at least one root outside the unit disk and yields a nondecaying or growing trajectory. Complex conjugate roots produce oscillation, with modulus \(\sqrt{\beta}\) when \(\beta>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar inertial mode is stable exactly under three Schur inequalities; crossing their boundary creates persistent oscillation or growth.
assumptions_latex: The recurrence is stationary and scalar.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to0\) for every initialization if and only if \(|\beta|<1\), \(q<1\), and \(1+q+2\beta>0\).

notation.meaning: eigenmode multiplier of the underlying fixed-point map

review_flags: Exact scalar Schur boundary requires an authoritative locator.

children.title: Anderson Variant Families

children.title: Type-I Anderson Acceleration
children.top_down_role: The inverse-model-oriented multisecant family.

knowledge_statements.title: Type-I Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse step obtained from a multisecant approximation of the residual Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(F(x)=G(x)-x\), choose \(x_0\), and let \(m_k\le k\). Form \(S_k=[x_{j+1}-x_j]\) and \(Y_k=[F(x_{j+1})-F(x_j)]\) over the last \(m_k\) steps. Type-I Anderson chooses a Jacobian model
\[B_k\in\arg\min_B\|B+I\|_F\quad\text{subject to}\quad B S_k=Y_k,\]
when these constraints are consistent and determine a usable nonsingular model, and updates \(x_{k+1}=x_k-B_k^{-1}F(x_k)\). If no history is retained, \(B_k=-I\) and the update reduces to \(x_{k+1}=G(x_k)\). Stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\) meets the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Type-I Anderson fits a residual-Jacobian model satisfying multisecant equations, then takes its inverse-model root-finding step.
assumptions_latex: The selected multisecant system admits a nonsingular model \(B_k\).
review_flags: Type-I sign and normalization conventions vary across references.
No Anderson-specific source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Type-I Anderson acceleration, but the sign, baseline model, and multisecant convention require an authoritative locator.

children.title: Type-II Anderson Acceleration
children.top_down_role: The residual-minimization-oriented family.

knowledge_statements.title: Type-II Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-minimizing Anderson form with an inverse multisecant model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(F(x)=G(x)-x\), choose \(x_0\), and retain \(m_k\le k\) recent difference pairs in matrices \(S_k\) and \(Y_k\). Compute
\[\gamma_k\in\arg\min_{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^{m_k}}\|F(x_k)-Y_k\gamma\|_2,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+F(x_k)-(S_k+Y_k)\gamma_k.\]
Equivalently, when \(Y_k\) has full column rank, set \(H_k=-I+(S_k+Y_k)(Y_k^\top Y_k)^{-1}Y_k^\top\); then \(H_kY_k=S_k\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k-H_kF(x_k)\). With \(m_k=0\), output the base step \(G(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Type-II Anderson minimizes the current residual over retained residual differences and applies the associated inverse multisecant step.
assumptions_latex: A least-squares minimizer \(\gamma_k\) is selected at each iteration.
review_flags: Type-II conventions should be matched to an authoritative Anderson reference.
No Anderson-specific source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-minimizing algorithm fits the Type-II container and is internally consistent, but its convention and equivalence lack supporting evidence.

children.title: Depth-One Anderson Methods
children.top_down_role: Low-memory Anderson variants with specialized analyses.

knowledge_statements.title: Depth-One Anderson Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-II Anderson acceleration retaining exactly one secant pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=G(x)-x\). For \(k\ge1\), define \(s_{k-1}=x_k-x_{k-1}\) and \(y_{k-1}=F(x_k)-F(x_{k-1})\). If \(y_{k-1}\ne0\), compute
\[\gamma_k=\frac{\langle y_{k-1},F(x_k)\rangle}{\|y_{k-1}\|_2^2},\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+F(x_k)-(s_{k-1}+y_{k-1})\gamma_k.\]
This is the depth-one Type-II least-squares update. If \(y_{k-1}=0\), use a declared safeguard, such as \(\gamma_k=0\), which returns the base fixed-point step. Stop according to a residual tolerance or iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Depth-one Anderson uses one iterate difference and one residual difference, giving a scalar least-squares coefficient and constant history storage.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean inner product defines the residual fit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(y_{k-1}\ne0\), the unique least-squares coefficient is \(\gamma_k=\langle y_{k-1},F(x_k)\rangle/\|y_{k-1}\|_2^2\).
review_flags: The depth-one formula is standard but lacks a supplied supporting locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The depth-one specialization is mathematically coherent and correctly classified as an algorithm, but no specific source locator supports it.

children.title: Anderson History-Depth Regimes
children.top_down_role: History-window regimes and their computational tradeoffs.

children.title: Limited-Memory Anderson Methods
children.top_down_role: Anderson variants retaining a bounded history window.

knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Memory Anderson Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sliding-window Anderson acceleration with a fixed maximum history depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a memory cap \(m\ge1\), let \(F=G-I\), and initialize \(x_0\). At iteration \(k\), set \(m_k=\min\{m,k\}\), form \(S_k\) and \(Y_k\) from the most recent \(m_k\) iterate and residual differences, solve
\[\gamma_k\in\arg\min_{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^{m_k}}\|F(x_k)-Y_k\gamma\|_2,\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+F(x_k)-(S_k+Y_k)\gamma_k\). Afterward discard every difference pair older than the newest \(m\). Terminate when the residual tolerance or iteration limit is reached; the output is the final iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limited-memory Anderson solves each residual fit using only the newest fixed number of secant pairs and discards older history.
assumptions_latex: The memory cap \(m\) is a fixed positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(m\) difference pairs participate in any Anderson least-squares problem.
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers limited-memory Anderson acceleration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sliding-window algorithm matches limited-memory Anderson methods, but no Anderson-specific source and locator are supplied.

children.title: Full-Memory Anderson Methods
children.top_down_role: Anderson variants retaining the complete available history.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Memory Anderson Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anderson acceleration retaining every secant pair generated since initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=G-I\) and initialize \(x_0\). At iteration \(k\ge1\), retain all differences \(s_j=x_{j+1}-x_j\) and \(y_j=F(x_{j+1})-F(x_j)\) for \(0\le j<k\), assemble \(S_k=[s_0,\ldots,s_{k-1}]\) and \(Y_k=[y_0,\ldots,y_{k-1}]\), and compute
\[\gamma_k\in\arg\min_{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^{k}}\|F(x_k)-Y_k\gamma\|_2.\]
Update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+F(x_k)-(S_k+Y_k)\gamma_k\). Stop at the prescribed residual tolerance or iteration limit; no history truncation occurs before termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-memory Anderson uses every previous secant pair, so the residual-fitting subspace grows by at most one dimension per iteration.
assumptions_latex: A least-squares minimizer is selected even if \(Y_k\) is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration uses history depth \(m_k=k\) and never discards a generated difference pair.
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers full-memory Anderson acceleration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly describes a full-history Type-II algorithm, but the claim has no supporting source locator.

children.title: History-Depth Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Accuracy, conditioning, storage, and work changes across history depths.

knowledge_statements.title: History-Depth Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic algebraic tradeoffs of increasing Type-II Anderson history depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an iteration \(k\) and nested residual-difference matrices \(Y_k^{(m)}\) whose columns correspond to histories of depths \(m=0,1,\ldots,k\). Define
\[\rho_m=\min_{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^{m}}\|F(x_k)-Y_k^{(m)}\gamma\|_2,\qquad \rho_0=\|F(x_k)\|_2.\]
Then \(\rho_{m+1}\le\rho_m\): enlarging the history cannot worsen the current unregularized least-squares fit. This monotonicity does not imply better conditioning or a smaller next residual; added columns may be nearly dependent. Storing dense history requires \(O(nm)\) numbers, while a generic dense least-squares solve requires \(O(nm^2+m^3)\) arithmetic without incremental factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: More history improves the current least-squares fit weakly, but increases storage and solve cost and may worsen conditioning or the actual next residual.
assumptions_latex: The depth-\(m\) column spaces are nested.
Residual fitting uses the unregularized Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{m+1}\le\rho_m\), while storage and generic dense solution costs grow with \(m\).
review_flags: Complexity convention and history tradeoff require a supporting numerical linear algebra locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested-subspace monotonicity is coherent, but the conditioning discussion and stated dense arithmetic bound require a specific numerical linear algebra or Anderson reference.

children.title: Stabilized Anderson Variant Family
children.top_down_role: Variants controlling aggressive or ill-conditioned extrapolation.

children.title: Damped Anderson Methods
children.top_down_role: Variants moderating the magnitude of accelerated corrections.

knowledge_statements.title: Damped Anderson Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation of an Anderson proposal toward the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p_k\) be an Anderson proposal computed from retained history, for example \(p_k=x_k+F(x_k)-(S_k+Y_k)\gamma_k\). Choose a damping parameter \(\theta_k\in(0,1]\) by a prescribed rule and update
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+\theta_k(p_k-x_k).\]
Thus \(\theta_k=1\) accepts the full accelerated proposal, whereas smaller \(\theta_k\) limits its displacement from \(x_k\). A safeguarded implementation may reduce \(\theta_k\) until a stated residual or merit-function acceptance test holds, and returns the accepted iterate; if no trial is accepted, it uses a declared fallback such as \(G(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Damped Anderson relaxes the accelerated proposal toward the current iterate, optionally reducing the damping until an acceptance test succeeds.
review_flags: Damped Anderson has multiple conventions; this record adopts proposal relaxation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Proposal relaxation is a valid damping mechanism and the algorithm kind fits, but terminology and safeguarding conventions require an authoritative locator.

children.title: Mixed Anderson Methods
children.top_down_role: Variants blending accelerated and baseline candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Anderson Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex mixing of the base fixed-point proposal and an accelerated Anderson proposal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), compute the base proposal \(b_k=G(x_k)\) and an Anderson proposal \(p_k\) from the retained history. Choose a mixing weight \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\) by a prescribed fixed or adaptive rule and set
\[x_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)b_k+\alpha_k p_k.\]
The endpoints give the base iteration when \(\alpha_k=0\) and the full Anderson proposal when \(\alpha_k=1\). An adaptive scheme may choose \(\alpha_k\) by minimizing or sufficiently decreasing a declared residual or merit model on this segment; if that test fails, it returns \(b_k\). Stop under the stated residual tolerance or iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed Anderson interpolates between the ordinary fixed-point proposal and the accelerated proposal, allowing rejection or partial use of acceleration.
assumptions_latex: Both \(b_k=G(x_k)\) and an Anderson proposal \(p_k\) are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) lies on the segment joining \(b_k\) and \(p_k\).
review_flags: The term mixed Anderson is convention-dependent; an authoritative source is needed to confirm this local sense.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed convex interpolation is coherent, but “mixed Anderson” is convention-dependent, so evidence is required to establish that this is the intended mathematical family.

children.title: Regularized Anderson Methods
children.top_down_role: Variants stabilizing ill-conditioned or noisy extrapolation subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Anderson Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tikhonov-regularized residual fitting for stable Anderson coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=G-I\), form retained difference matrices \(S_k,Y_k\), and choose \(\lambda_k>0\). Compute
\[\gamma_k=\arg\min_{\gamma}\bigl\{\|F(x_k)-Y_k\gamma\|_2^2+\lambda_k\|\gamma\|_2^2\bigr\}=(Y_k^\top Y_k+\lambda_k I)^{-1}Y_k^\top F(x_k),\]
then update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+F(x_k)-(S_k+Y_k)\gamma_k\). The coefficient is uniquely defined even when \(Y_k\) is rank deficient because \(Y_k^\top Y_k+\lambda_k I\) is positive definite. A complete implementation specifies how \(\lambda_k\) is chosen and stops at a residual tolerance or iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized Anderson penalizes large mixing coefficients, yielding a unique, better-conditioned coefficient solve even with rank-deficient residual history.
assumptions_latex: The retained matrices \(S_k,Y_k\) have the same number of columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized coefficient \(\gamma_k\) exists uniquely and satisfies \((Y_k^\top Y_k+\lambda_k I)\gamma_k=Y_k^\top F(x_k)\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator covers regularized Anderson acceleration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Tikhonov-regularized coefficient problem is precise and appropriately classified as an algorithm, but no supporting Anderson-specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Stabilization Mechanism Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Structural tradeoffs among damping, mixing, and regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Mechanism Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic comparison of damping, proposal mixing, and coefficient regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an Anderson proposal \(p_k\), damping gives \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\theta_k(p_k-x_k)\), so its displacement is scaled exactly by \(\theta_k\). Mixing with \(b_k=G(x_k)\) gives \(x_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)b_k+\alpha_kp_k\), constraining the iterate to the proposal segment when \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\). Neither operation changes the conditioning of the coefficient fit used to construct \(p_k\). By contrast, Tikhonov regularization replaces \(Y_k^\top Y_k\) by \(Y_k^\top Y_k+\lambda_kI\); for \(\lambda_k>0\), its smallest eigenvalue is at least \(\lambda_k\), although the resulting proposal need not satisfy any residual-decrease test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Damping limits displacement, mixing interpolates with the base proposal, and regularization conditions the coefficient solve; these mechanisms provide different safeguards.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient fit uses the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Damping and mixing control the accepted step, whereas regularization directly makes \(Y_k^\top Y_k+\lambda_kI\) positive definite.
review_flags: Comparison is algebraically checkable but lacks a supplied stabilization-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property appropriately distinguishes step damping, proposal mixing, and coefficient regularization, but the comparison lacks a stabilization-specific source.

children.title: Equivalent Views of Anderson Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Representations connecting Anderson acceleration to residual minimization, multisecant updates, and Krylov methods.

children.title: Residual-Minimization View
children.top_down_role: Residual fitting as the organizing representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Minimization View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-II Anderson represented as projection of the current residual onto residual-difference history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=G-I\), and let \(Y_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m_k}\) contain retained residual differences. The Type-II coefficient satisfies
\[\gamma_k\in\arg\min_\gamma\|F(x_k)-Y_k\gamma\|_2,
\qquad r_k^{\mathrm{fit}}=F(x_k)-Y_k\gamma_k.\]
Consequently, \(r_k^{\mathrm{fit}}\) is the orthogonal projection of \(F(x_k)\) onto \(\operatorname{range}(Y_k)^\perp\), equivalently \(Y_k^\top r_k^{\mathrm{fit}}=0\). The associated iterate is
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+F(x_k)-(S_k+Y_k)\gamma_k.\]
The minimized quantity is a fitted linearized residual; without additional assumptions it is not equal to the nonlinear residual \(F(x_{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Type-II Anderson orthogonally removes from the current residual the component represented by stored residual differences, then applies the corresponding secant correction.
assumptions_latex: Residual fitting uses the Euclidean norm.

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the residual-difference matrix

review_flags: No supplied locator supports the Anderson residual-minimization representation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection formulation is internally consistent and fits the representation container, but no source locator supports its identification with the Type-II Anderson view.

children.title: Multisecant Quasi-Newton View
children.top_down_role: Secant-model interpretations of Anderson histories.

knowledge_statements.title: Multisecant Quasi-Newton View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-II Anderson acceleration represented as an inverse multisecant update for the fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=G(x)-x\), \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\), and \(y_i=f(x_{i+1})-f(x_i)\). Form \(S_k=[s_i]_{i\in I_k}\) and \(Y_k=[y_i]_{i\in I_k}\), and assume \(Y_k\) has full column rank. The matrix
\[
H_k=-I+(S_k+Y_k)(Y_k^{\mathsf T}Y_k)^{-1}Y_k^{\mathsf T}
\]
satisfies the multisecant equations \(H_kY_k=S_k\). Consequently, the undamped Type-II Anderson update obtained from \(\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma}\|f(x_k)-Y_k\gamma\|_2\) can be written equivalently as
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-H_kf(x_k)=G(x_k)-(S_k+Y_k)\gamma_k.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Type-II Anderson acceleration is an inverse quasi-Newton step whose approximate inverse residual Jacobian satisfies every retained secant equation.
assumptions_latex: \(G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) and all retained iterates are defined.
The least-squares norm is Euclidean and the mixing parameter equals one.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Type-II Anderson multisecant identity derived from its least-squares update

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic multisecant identity is internally consistent, and representation is the correct knowledge kind, but no inspectable Anderson-specific source supports the stated Type-II convention and update equivalence.

children.title: Linear Krylov Equivalences
children.top_down_role: Linear-problem equivalences and the conditions under which they cease to hold.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Anderson Acceleration for Fixed-Point Iterations
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Untruncated linear problems and GMRES equivalence
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Anderson Acceleration for Fixed-Point Iterations

children.title: GMRES Equivalence of Type-II Anderson Acceleration
children.top_down_role: The residual-minimizing linear equivalence family.

knowledge_statements.title: GMRES Equivalence of Type-II Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic, full-history equivalence for an affine fixed-point map, stated at the residual-minimizing extrapolate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(x)=Ax+b\), put \(M=I-A\), and consider \(Mx=b\) from \(x_0\). In exact arithmetic, run undamped full-history Type-II Anderson acceleration and define its affine extrapolate by
\[
\bar x_k=\sum_{i=0}^{k}\alpha_i x_i,
\qquad
\sum_{i=0}^{k}\alpha_i=1,
\qquad
\alpha\in\operatorname*{argmin}\left\|\sum_{i=0}^{k}\alpha_i(b-Mx_i)\right\|_2.
\]
If the generated Krylov dimension increases through step \(k\), then \(\bar x_k\) is the \(k\)-th GMRES iterate: it minimizes \(\|b-Mx\|_2\) over \(x_0+\mathcal K_k(M,r_0)\). The next Anderson iterate satisfies \(x_{k+1}=G(\bar x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linear fixed-point problem, the full-history Type-II Anderson extrapolate is the corresponding GMRES residual minimizer; Anderson then applies the fixed-point map.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic is exact, history is full, and mixing is undamped and unregularized.
The Krylov process does not stagnate or break down through step \(k\).

notation.meaning: Linear-system matrix induced by the affine fixed-point map.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical full-memory Anderson–GMRES correspondence for affine maps
indexing and nonstagnation formulation require an Anderson-specific theorem locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the terminal container, but the exact iterate indexing and sufficient nonstagnation or breakdown hypotheses for the full-history Type-II Anderson–GMRES equivalence require an authoritative theorem locator.

children.title: Arnoldi Equivalence of Type-I Anderson Acceleration
children.top_down_role: The full-orthogonalization linear equivalence family.

knowledge_statements.title: Arnoldi Equivalence of Type-I Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic subspace correspondence for full-history Type-I Anderson acceleration on affine maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(x)=Ax+b\), \(M=I-A\), and \(r_0=b-Mx_0\). Run full-history, undamped Type-I Anderson acceleration in exact arithmetic, using nonsingular Type-I Gram systems and no regularization. If no rank breakdown occurs through step \(k\), then the successively generated residual-difference directions span the Arnoldi Krylov spaces:
\[
\operatorname{span}\{y_0,\ldots,y_{k-1}\}=M\mathcal K_k(M,r_0).
\]
After normalization and orthogonalization, these directions generate the same nested Krylov subspaces as Arnoldi applied to \(M\) with starting vector \(r_0\). Thus Type-I Anderson’s multisecant construction is a nonorthogonal full-orthogonalization realization of the Arnoldi subspace process, up to nonsingular changes of basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On affine problems, full-history Type-I Anderson and Arnoldi generate the same nested Krylov subspaces, although their basis vectors may differ.
assumptions_latex: Type-I Anderson uses full history, unit mixing, exact arithmetic, and no regularization.
All Type-I Gram matrices remain nonsingular through step \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{span}\{y_0,\ldots,y_{k-1}\}=M\mathcal K_k(M,r_0)\), up to nonsingular basis transformations.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Type-I Anderson is commonly interpreted through an Arnoldi-type multisecant process
precise basis and indexing identity requires a dedicated source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Theorem is the appropriate kind, but the displayed identity gives the shifted space M K_k(M,r_0), which is not generally the same space as the order-k Arnoldi space K_k(M,r_0). A dedicated source is required to determine the correct indexing and precise Type-I correspondence.

children.title: Finite-History Krylov Equivalence Boundary
children.top_down_role: Departures from full-history Krylov equivalences.

children.title: Truncated-History Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Krylov correspondences retained or lost under bounded history.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated-History Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed residual minimization expressed over the affine space generated by retained Anderson differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), retain indices \(I_k\) with \(|I_k|\le m\), and form \(S_k=[s_i]_{i\in I_k}\) and \(Y_k=[y_i]_{i\in I_k}\). For an affine residual \(r(x)=b-Mx\), the truncated Type-II fitting problem
\[
\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma}\|r(x_k)-Y_k\gamma\|_2
\]
is exactly the minimum-residual problem over the retained affine correction space:
\[
\bar x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in x_k+\operatorname{range}(S_k)}\|b-Mx\|_2,
\qquad
\bar x_k=x_k-S_k\gamma_k,
\]
provided \(Y_k=-MS_k\). This is a local retained-subspace equivalence; it does not assert equality with full GMRES or with a restarted Krylov method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated Anderson fitting is minimum-residual projection over the span of retained steps, but this local identity does not imply full-GMRES equivalence.
assumptions_latex: The same Euclidean norm is used in both minimization problems.

notation.meaning: Indices retained in the current history window.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct affine least-squares change of variables
source needed for the intended finite-history Anderson formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The retained-subspace least-squares identity is algebraically consistent and representation fits the leaf, but an inspectable source is needed to establish that this is the intended truncated Type-II Anderson formulation.

children.title: Restarted Krylov Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Correspondences between restarted acceleration and restarted Krylov behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Restarted Krylov Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which block-reset Type-II Anderson corresponds to restarted GMRES.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(G(x)=Ax+b\) and \(M=I-A\), a restarted-Krylov correspondence holds when Anderson history is completely discarded at prescribed restart indices \(0=t_0<t_1<\cdots\), each block uses full history relative to \(x_{t_j}\), and the Type-II fit is undamped, unregularized, and computed in exact arithmetic. If no stagnation occurs inside a block of length at most \(m\), its Anderson extrapolates are the GMRES residual minimizers over
\[
x_{t_j}+\mathcal K_\ell(M,r_{t_j}),
\qquad 0\le \ell\le m.
\]
Therefore block-reset Anderson corresponds to GMRES restarted from the block residual. A sliding window that drops only the oldest column does not satisfy this condition in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anderson matches restarted GMRES when its entire history is reset at matching block boundaries; ordinary sliding-window truncation is generally different.
assumptions_latex: The fixed-point map is affine and arithmetic is exact.
Each restart discards all earlier Anderson columns.
Each block uses full, undamped, unregularized Type-II history without stagnation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Within block \(j\), the extrapolate minimizes \(\|b-Mx\|_2\) over \(x_{t_j}+\mathcal K_\ell(M,r_{t_j})\).

notation.meaning: Beginning index of restart block j.
Maximum number of Krylov steps per block.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: blockwise application of the full-history Anderson–GMRES correspondence
exact restart indexing requires source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is an appropriate kind, but the exact block-reset correspondence, restart indexing, and within-block hypotheses depend on the unsourced full-history Anderson–GMRES theorem.

children.title: Full-History Departure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where limited history or restarts invalidate complete-history equivalences.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-History Departure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mechanisms that invalidate exact full-history Anderson–Krylov equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exact full-history linear Krylov equivalences require an affine map, complete unrestarted history, exact arithmetic, a fixed Euclidean residual metric, unit mixing, no regularization, and no rank breakdown. The equivalence need not persist if any of the following occurs: \(G\) is nonlinear; columns are truncated, filtered, or recycled; damping changes the update; regularization changes the least-squares minimizer; the metric varies with \(k\); finite precision destroys the predicted span; or a retained difference matrix loses rank. In these regimes Anderson may still be interpreted as a local multisecant or residual-fitting method, but equality with the corresponding full-history GMRES or Arnoldi iterates is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinearity, truncation, damping, regularization, changing metrics, roundoff, or rank loss can destroy exact full-history Anderson–Krylov equivalence.
assumptions_latex: The reference equivalence is the exact-arithmetic, affine, full-history Anderson–Krylov correspondence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing any listed structural assumption eliminates the general guarantee of iterate-by-iterate Krylov equivalence.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: each listed modification changes an algebraic hypothesis used by exact linear equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary fits the container and the cautious 'need not persist' language avoids claiming failure in every instance, but the complete list of necessary conditions and departure mechanisms lacks an authoritative locator.

children.title: Anderson Numerical Realization
children.top_down_role: Linear-algebra and history-management mechanisms governing robustness, storage, and cost.
