children.title: Geometry-Dependent Selection
children.top_down_role: Solution-selection behavior shaped by the ambient normed-space geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Dependent Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The Halpern-selected fixed point is characterized by the ambient space’s projection or duality geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\operatorname{Fix}T\) be a nonempty closed convex fixed-point set and let \(u\) be the Halpern anchor. The selected limit must be expressed using the ambient geometry. In a Hilbert space it is the metric projection \(q=P_Fu\), equivalently
\[
\langle u-q,z-q\rangle\leq0\qquad(z\in F).
\]
In a smooth Banach-space regime with normalized duality map \(J\) and sunny nonexpansive retraction \(Q_F\), the corresponding candidate is \(q=Q_Fu\), characterized by
\[
\langle u-q,J(z-q)\rangle\leq0\qquad(z\in F).
\]
Consequently, the selection statement and its hypotheses must change with the geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Halpern selection uses metric projection in Hilbert spaces and a duality-map or sunny-retraction characterization in suitable Banach spaces.
assumptions_latex: In the Banach case, smoothness and retraction hypotheses make \(J\) and \(Q_F\) well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected point is \(P_Fu\) in Hilbert geometry and \(Q_Fu\) in the stated smooth Banach geometry.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hilbert characterization is standard, but the Banach-space variational characterization and conclusion depend on precise smoothness, duality-map, convexity, and sunny-retraction hypotheses that are not supplied or cited.

children.title: Affine Nonexpansive Regime
children.top_down_role: The specialization admitting sharper polynomial and worst-case structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Nonexpansive Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial representation of Halpern iterates for affine nonexpansive mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and \(T(x)=Ax+b\), where \(A:H\to H\) is bounded linear with \(\lVert A\rVert\leq1\). For \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)T(x_k)\), every iterate has the affine-polynomial representation
\[
x_k=P_k(A)x_0+Q_k(A)u+R_k(A)b.
\]
Here \(P_0=I\), \(Q_0=R_0=0\), and
\[
P_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)AP_k,
\quad Q_{k+1}=\alpha_kI+(1-\alpha_k)AQ_k,
\quad R_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)(AR_k+I).
\]
Thus schedule design becomes the selection of scalar coefficients in operator polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine nonexpansive map, each Halpern iterate is an explicitly recursive operator-polynomial combination of the initial point, anchor, and translation.
assumptions_latex: \(T(x)=Ax+b\) on a Hilbert space and \(\lVert A\rVert\leq1\).

notation.meaning: linear and translation parts of T
operator polynomials determined by the schedule

children.title: Contractive Regime
children.top_down_role: The regime connecting anchored and direct Picard phases.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractive Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error recursion and transition from anchored Halpern steps to geometric Picard convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\) satisfy \(\|Tx-Ty\|\le q\|x-y\|\) for some \(q\in[0,1)\), and let \(p\) be its unique fixed point. For an anchor \(u\in H\), define \(x_{n+1}=\alpha_nu+(1-\alpha_n)Tx_n\), where \(0\le\alpha_n\le1\). Then
\[
\|x_{n+1}-p\|\le \alpha_n\|u-p\|+(1-\alpha_n)q\|x_n-p\|.
\]
Consequently, \(\alpha_n\to0\) implies \(x_n\to p\). If anchoring is discontinued after index \(m\), so that \(x_{n+1}=Tx_n\) for \(n\ge m\), then \(\|x_n-p\|\le q^{n-m}\|x_m-p\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive map absorbs a vanishing anchor perturbation; after switching to ordinary Picard iteration, the remaining error decreases geometrically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_n\to0\Rightarrow x_n\to p\), and direct Picard steps after \(m\) satisfy \(\|x_n-p\|\le q^{n-m}\|x_m-p\|\).

notation.meaning: the unique fixed point of the contraction

children.title: Common Fixed-Point Regime
children.top_down_role: Anchored approximation for families of fixed-point maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Common Fixed-Point Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical Halpern iteration for a controlled family sharing a fixed-point set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and let \((T_i)_{i\in I}\) be nonexpansive maps \(T_i:H\to H\) with nonempty common fixed-point set \(F=\bigcap_{i\in I}\operatorname{Fix}T_i\). Given an anchor \(u\in H\), an initial point \(x_0\in H\), controls \(\alpha_n\in(0,1)\), and indices \(i_n\in I\), perform
\[
x_{n+1}=\alpha_nu+(1-\alpha_n)T_{i_n}x_n,
\qquad n=0,1,\ldots,N-1.
\]
Return \(x_N\). Convergence requires an additional coverage or regularity condition on \((i_n)\) ensuring that asymptotic invariance under the selected maps identifies points of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each step applies one member of a nonexpansive family and averages its value with a fixed anchor; the family must share fixed points.
assumptions_latex: \(T_i:H\to H\) is nonexpansive for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_N\) is the output of the recursion \(x_{n+1}=\alpha_nu+(1-\alpha_n)T_{i_n}x_n\).

notation.meaning: the operator selected at iteration n

children.title: Stochastic Halpern Regime
children.top_down_role: Anchored iteration under noisy or sampled operator access.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Halpern Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Halpern iteration with conditionally unbiased, bounded-variance operator estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive, and suppose a stochastic oracle returns \(G(x,\xi_n)\in H\). Given \(u,x_0\in H\), controls \(\alpha_n\in(0,1)\), and a filtration \((\mathcal F_n)\), sample \(\xi_n\) and update
\[
x_{n+1}=\alpha_nu+(1-\alpha_n)G(x_n,\xi_n),
\qquad n=0,1,\ldots,N-1.
\]
The oracle regime is specified by \(\mathbb E[G(x_n,\xi_n)\mid\mathcal F_n]=Tx_n\) and \(\mathbb E[\|G(x_n,\xi_n)-Tx_n\|^2\mid\mathcal F_n]\le\sigma_n^2\). Return the last iterate \(x_N\), or a prescribed average when the associated convergence theorem requires averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic Halpern step anchors an unbiased noisy operator evaluation; its analysis depends on the conditional variance sequence and control weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_N\) is generated by \(x_{n+1}=\alpha_nu+(1-\alpha_n)G(x_n,\xi_n)\) under conditionally unbiased noisy access.

notation.meaning: a stochastic estimate of the operator value
the information available before the nth oracle sample

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and conditional oracle model fit the stochastic regime, but an authoritative source is required to support this precise stochastic Halpern formulation and its permissible outputs.

children.title: Halpern Landmark Theory
children.top_down_role: Major theorem families for strong convergence, selection, residual complexity, and worst-case optimality.

children.title: Strong Convergence Families
children.top_down_role: Strong-convergence results across classical Halpern regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convergence Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Hilbert-space strong convergence under bounded-variation Halpern controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a Hilbert space \(H\), let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive with \(F=\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\), and let \(u,x_0\in C\). Define \(x_{n+1}=\alpha_nu+(1-\alpha_n)Tx_n\). If \(0<\alpha_n<1\), \(\alpha_n\to0\), \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\alpha_n=\infty\), and \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}|\alpha_{n+1}-\alpha_n|<\infty\), then the iterates converge strongly:
\[
x_n\longrightarrow P_Fu.
\]
Thus the limit is a fixed point selected by the anchor rather than an unspecified weak cluster point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under classical vanishing, nonsummable, bounded-variation weights, Halpern iterates converge in norm to the fixed point nearest the anchor.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex; \(T:C\to C\) is nonexpansive with \(F\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: the metric projection of the anchor onto F

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a standard strong-convergence theorem with sufficient classical bounded-variation controls, and theorem is the correct content kind, but no inspectable theorem or section citation is supplied.

children.title: Anchor-Dependent Fixed-Point Selection
children.top_down_role: Anchor-dependent solution-selection results.

children.title: Best-Approximation Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection of a fixed point relative to a prescribed anchor.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Approximation Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-projection characterization of the fixed point selected by strong Halpern convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\), \(C\), \(T\), \(F=\operatorname{Fix}T\), and \((x_n)\) satisfy the hypotheses of the classical strong-convergence Halpern theorem with anchor \(u\in C\). Then
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}x_n=P_Fu,
\qquad
\|u-P_Fu\|=\min_{z\in F}\|u-z\|.
\]
Because \(F\) is closed and convex, \(P_Fu\) is unique. Equivalently, it is characterized by
\[
\langle u-P_Fu,z-P_Fu\rangle\le0
\quad\text{for every }z\in F.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strongly convergent Halpern sequence selects the unique fixed point closest to its anchor, characterized by the Hilbert-space projection inequality.
assumptions_latex: The Halpern controls satisfy a valid strong-convergence theorem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection characterization is mathematically consistent with the prerequisite strong-convergence theorem and fits the selection property container, but it lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Minimum-Norm Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection of a fixed point according to norm minimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Norm Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-norm fixed-point selection obtained when the anchor is the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and let \(F\subset H\) be the nonempty closed convex fixed-point set of a nonexpansive map. If a Halpern iteration converges strongly with anchor \(u=0\), then
\[
\bar x=P_F0
=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in F}\|z\|.
\]
The minimizer is unique and satisfies the variational inequality
\[
\langle \bar x,z-\bar x\rangle\ge0
\quad\text{for every }z\in F.
\]
Hence zero anchoring selects the minimum-norm solution whenever the underlying fixed-point formulation has multiple solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the origin as anchor, strong Halpern convergence selects the unique fixed point of minimum Hilbert norm.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The Halpern sequence converges strongly to \(P_Fu\).

notation.meaning: the projection of the origin onto F

children.title: Anchor-Dependent Selection
children.top_down_role: Dependence of the selected fixed point on the anchoring reference.

knowledge_statements.title: Anchor-Dependent Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence and stability of the selected fixed point as the anchor varies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a Hilbert space \(H\). Suppose two Halpern sequences for the same nonexpansive map satisfy a strong-convergence theorem, with anchors \(u,v\in H\), respectively. Their limits are \(P_Fu\) and \(P_Fv\), and the projection map is firmly nonexpansive:
\[
\|P_Fu-P_Fv\|^2
\le \langle P_Fu-P_Fv,u-v\rangle
\le \|P_Fu-P_Fv\|\,\|u-v\|.
\]
In particular, \(\|P_Fu-P_Fv\|\le\|u-v\|\); changing the anchor can change the selected fixed point but cannot amplify the anchor displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different anchors select their corresponding nearest fixed points, and the selected limit changes no faster than the anchor itself.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Both Halpern sequences satisfy strong convergence to their anchor projections.

notation.meaning: the Halpern sequence with anchor u

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The firm-nonexpansiveness inequality and anchor-dependent projection conclusion are correct and fit the property container, but no inspectable source supports the selection and stability claim.

children.title: Zero-Anchor Specialization
children.top_down_role: The minimum-norm selection regime associated with a zero anchor.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Anchor Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Halpern recursion specialized to the origin anchor and minimum-norm selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a closed convex subset of a Hilbert space \(H\) with \(0\in C\), let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive, and choose \(x_0\in C\). For controls \(\alpha_n\in(0,1)\), perform
\[
x_{n+1}=(1-\alpha_n)Tx_n,
\qquad n=0,1,\ldots,N-1.
\]
Return \(x_N\). If \(F=\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\), \(\alpha_n\to0\), \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\alpha_n=\infty\), and \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}|\alpha_{n+1}-\alpha_n|<\infty\), then the infinite sequence converges in norm to \(P_F0\), the minimum-norm fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Setting the anchor to zero removes the additive anchor term; under classical vanishing, nonsummable, bounded-variation controls, the iterates converge to the minimum-norm fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset H\) is closed and convex with \(0\in C\).

children.title: Accelerated Fixed-Point Residual Complexity
children.top_down_role: Nonasymptotic residual guarantees for anchored iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Fixed-Point Residual Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An \(O(1/N)\) last-iterate residual bound for the canonical Halpern schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive on a Hilbert space, let \(p\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), and initialize at the anchor \(x_0=u\). For \(n\ge0\), set
\[
x_{n+1}=\frac{1}{n+2}u+\frac{n+1}{n+2}Tx_n.
\]
After \(N\) operator evaluations, the last iterate satisfies
\[
\|x_N-Tx_N\|\le\frac{2\|u-p\|}{N+1}.
\]
Thus, if \(R\ge\|u-p\|\), residual accuracy \(\|x_N-Tx_N\|\le\varepsilon\) is achieved with \(N\ge\lceil2R/\varepsilon\rceil-1\) evaluations of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical Halpern weights yield a last-iterate fixed-point residual of order one over the number of operator evaluations.

notation.meaning: an upper bound on the anchor-to-fixed-point distance

children.title: Minimax Optimality of Halpern Iteration
children.top_down_role: Worst-case optimality and matching lower-bound families.

children.title: General Nonexpansive Optimality
children.top_down_role: Worst-case optimality for general nonexpansive maps.

knowledge_statements.title: General Nonexpansive Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-optimal residual complexity in a deterministic nonexpansive-operator oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider deterministic algorithms that access an unknown nonexpansive map \(T\) only through sequential evaluations and whose query points lie in the affine span of the anchor and previously returned oracle values. Assume some fixed point \(p\) satisfies \(\|u-p\|\le R\). There exist universal constants \(c,C>0\) such that the minimax last-iterate residual after \(N\) evaluations obeys
\[
\frac{cR}{N+1}
\le
\inf_{	ext{algorithms}}\sup_T\|x_N-Tx_N\|
\le
\frac{CR}{N+1}.
\]
The upper bound is attained in order by Halpern iteration; therefore its \(O(R/\varepsilon)\) oracle complexity is minimax order-optimal in this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within the stated deterministic oracle model, no method uniformly improves the Halpern residual order of one over the iteration count.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) ranges over nonexpansive maps having a fixed point within distance \(R\) of the anchor.
The algorithm uses \(N\) sequential operator evaluations.
Queries obey the stated affine-span oracle restriction.

notation.meaning: the initial radius to a fixed point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the optimality container, but the minimax class, affine-span restriction, and universal lower bound are specialized claims requiring an authoritative theorem locator.

children.title: Affine-Map Optimality
children.top_down_role: Sharper optimality structure for affine maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Map Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial minimax representation for self-adjoint affine nonexpansive fixed-point maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T(x)=Ax+b\) on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, where \(A=A^*\), \(\|A\|\le1\), and \(p=Ap+b\). For any polynomial affine-oracle method whose error after \(N\) evaluations has the form \(x_N-p=q_N(A)(x_0-p)\), consistency at the fixed mode requires \(q_N(1)=1\). Its worst-case residual over this affine class is represented by
\[
R\max_{\lambda\in[-1,1]}|(1-\lambda)q_N(\lambda)|.
\]
Consequently, the optimal worst-case affine residual equals
\[
R\inf_{q\in\mathcal P_N,\ q(1)=1}
\max_{\lambda\in[-1,1]}|(1-\lambda)q(\lambda)|.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For self-adjoint affine maps, residual optimality reduces exactly to a scalar minimax-polynomial problem over the spectrum.

notation.meaning: polynomials of degree at most N
the error polynomial of the oracle method
the self-adjoint linear part of the affine map

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind is appropriate for the proposed spectral reduction, but the admissible polynomial-oracle class, normalization, and exact minimax equality require a precise source.

children.title: Mann-Iteration Lower-Bound Boundary
children.top_down_role: The worst-case separation between Halpern and classical Mann families.

knowledge_statements.title: Mann-Iteration Lower-Bound Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit shift example separating classical constant-relaxation Mann iteration from the Halpern \(O(1/N)\) rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S:\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\to\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\) be the unilateral shift \(Se_j=e_{j+1}\), whose unique fixed point is \(0\). Fix \(\beta\in(0,1)\), take \(x_0=e_0\), and run the Mann iteration
\[
x_{n+1}=(1-\beta)x_n+\beta Sx_n.
\]
Then
\[
x_n=\sum_{j=0}^n\binom nj(1-\beta)^{n-j}\beta^j e_j,
\qquad
\|x_n-Sx_n\|=\Theta_\beta(n^{-3/4}).
\]
Hence constant-relaxation Mann iteration has no uniform \(O(1/n)\) residual guarantee, even for a linear isometry with a fixed point, whereas Halpern anchoring can attain that order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the unilateral shift, constant-relaxation Mann residuals decay as order n to the minus three quarters, excluding a uniform one-over-n guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_n-Sx_n\|=\Theta_\beta(n^{-3/4})\), so this Mann family does not admit a uniform \(O(1/n)\) residual bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and constant-relaxation scope fit the container, but the exact shift residual asymptotic and resulting lower-bound separation require an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator Fixed-Point Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm certificate for an approximate fixed point of a single-valued operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(D\subseteq X\), and let \(T:D\to X\). The fixed-point residual at \(x\in D\) is \(r_T(x):=x-Tx\). For \(\varepsilon\geq 0\), the pair \((x,r_T(x))\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-fixed-point certificate when \(\|r_T(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\). This certificate is directly verifiable with one evaluation of \(T\), and \(r_T(x)=0\) holds exactly when \(x\in\operatorname{Fix}T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The displacement between a point and its operator image certifies approximate fixed-point accuracy; zero displacement is equivalent to being a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(D\subseteq X\).

notation.meaning: set of fixed points of T

knowledge_statements.title: Natural-Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Natural residual for a constrained variational inequality in a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(C\subseteq H\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(F:C\to H\). For \(\gamma>0\), define \(R_\gamma(x):=\gamma^{-1}\bigl(x-P_C(x-\gamma F(x))\bigr)\). Then \(\|R_\gamma(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) is a directly computable natural-residual certificate. Moreover, \(R_\gamma(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) solves \(\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\) for every \(y\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled projected step measures variational-inequality stationarity, and it vanishes exactly at a solution.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space and \(C\subseteq H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Mapping Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal-gradient stationarity certificate for convex composite minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to\mathbb R\) be convex and Fréchet differentiable, and let \(g:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For \(\gamma>0\), define \(G_\gamma(x):=\gamma^{-1}\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x-\gamma\nabla f(x))\bigr)\). The bound \(\|G_\gamma(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies proximal-gradient stationarity, while \(G_\gamma(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x)\), equivalently \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(f+g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled proximal-gradient displacement is a computable stationarity certificate and vanishes exactly at a composite convex minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and Fréchet differentiable on the Hilbert space \(H\).
\(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

notation.meaning: proximity operator of gamma times g

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone-Inclusion Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent certificate for a zero of a maximally monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone, and let \(\gamma>0\). For \(x\in H\), set \(y:=J_{\gamma A}x\) and \(r_\gamma(x):=\gamma^{-1}(x-y)\). The resolvent identity gives \(r_\gamma(x)\in Ay\). Hence \(\|r_\gamma(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies an explicit graph point \((y,r_\gamma(x))\in\operatorname{gra}A\) with inclusion residual at most \(\varepsilon\); moreover, \(r_\gamma(x)=0\) exactly when \(0\in Ax\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resolvent evaluation produces a graph point whose second component certifies approximate satisfaction of a monotone inclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Splitting-Map Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic certificate induced by a fixed-point representation of a splitting method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(Z\) be a set, and let \(\mathcal S\subseteq Z\) be the solution set of a target inclusion. Suppose a splitting construction provides a single-valued map \(T:H\to H\) and a computable recovery map \(S:H\to Z\) satisfying \(S(\operatorname{Fix}T)\subseteq\mathcal S\). For \(x\in H\) and \(\lambda>0\), define \(r_{T,\lambda}(x):=\lambda^{-1}(x-Tx)\). The tuple \((x,Tx,Sx,r_{T,\lambda}(x))\) is verifiable by evaluating \(T\) and \(S\), and \(\|r_{T,\lambda}(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) is the associated splitting-map residual certificate. If \(r_{T,\lambda}(x)=0\), then \(Sx\in\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A splitting fixed-point map supplies a computable displacement certificate, while a specified recovery map converts an exact fixed point into a solution of the represented inclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space, \(Z\) is a set, and \(\mathcal S\subseteq Z\) is the target solution set.
\(S:H\to Z\) is computable and satisfies \(S(\operatorname{Fix}T)\subseteq\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|r_{T,\lambda}(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) is a splitting-map residual certificate, and \(r_{T,\lambda}(x)=0\Rightarrow Sx\in\mathcal S\).

notation.meaning: solution set of the represented inclusion

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal KKT certificate for a convex composite primal–dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) and \(Y\) be Hilbert spaces, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(K:H\to Y\) be bounded linear. For \(x\in H\), \(y\in Y\), and \(\tau,\sigma>0\), define \(r_x:=\tau^{-1}\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x-\tau K^*y)\bigr)\) and \(r_y:=\sigma^{-1}\bigl(y-\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y+\sigma Kx)\bigr)\). Then \(\bigl(\|r_x\|^2+\|r_y\|^2\bigr)^{1/2}\leq\varepsilon\) is a computable primal–dual residual certificate, and \(r_x=r_y=0\) if and only if \(-K^*y\in\partial f(x)\) and \(Kx\in\partial g^*(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex composite primal–dual pair, two proximal displacements jointly form a computable KKT certificate and vanish exactly when both KKT inclusions hold.
assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral feasibility certificate for consensus over a connected undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a connected undirected graph with oriented incidence matrix \(B\), and let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n\). Define \(r_{\mathrm{con}}(x):=(B\otimes I_d)x\). Then \(r_{\mathrm{con}}(x)=0\) if and only if \(x_1=\cdots=x_n\). If \(\sigma_+(B)\) denotes the smallest positive singular value of \(B\) and \(P_{\mathrm{con}}\) the orthogonal projection onto the consensus subspace, then \(\|x-P_{\mathrm{con}}x\|\leq\sigma_+(B)^{-1}\|r_{\mathrm{con}}(x)\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edge disagreements vanish exactly at consensus and, through the graph spectral gap, bound distance to the consensus subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a connected undirected graph with incidence matrix \(B\).

notation.meaning: smallest positive singular value of B

children.title: Ergodic Residual Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate formed from weighted averages of residual-bearing iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed vector space, let \(D\subseteq X\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(T:D\to X\) be single-valued. Given \(x_0,\ldots,x_{N-1}\in D\) and weights \(w_k\geq0\) with \(W_N:=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k>0\), define \(\bar x_N:=W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_kx_k\) and \(\bar r_N:=W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k(x_k-Tx_k)\). An ergodic residual certificate reports \((\bar x_N,\bar r_N)\) with \(\|\bar r_N\|\leq\varepsilon\). It certifies the averaged residual vector, but without additional structure it does not certify \(\|\bar x_N-T\bar x_N\|\) or the residual of any individual sampled point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ergodic certificate bounds a weighted average of residual vectors; it does not automatically bound the operator residual at the averaged point or at any sampled iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed vector space and \(D\subseteq X\) is nonempty and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\bar r_N\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies only the displayed weighted-average residual unless additional structure supplies a translation to a pointwise residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate attached to one actual iterate or explicitly selected output point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:D\to X\) be a fixed-point map on a normed space, and let \(x_0,\ldots,x_N\in D\) be computed iterates. A pointwise residual certificate consists of an index \(j\in\{0,\ldots,N\}\), the output \(x_j\), and the verifiable residual \(r_j:=x_j-Tx_j\), with \(\|r_j\|\leq\varepsilon\). A best-iterate convention chooses \(j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\leq k\leq N}\|x_k-Tx_k\|\); a last-iterate convention fixes \(j=N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise certificate identifies one computed iterate and directly bounds that iterate's fixed-point residual.

children.title: Ergodic-to-Pointwise Separation

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic-to-Pointwise Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-vector averaging can conceal uniformly nonzero pointwise residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), let \(T=-I\), choose \(a\neq0\), and generate \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k\) from \(x_0=a\). Then \(x_k=(-1)^ka\) and \(x_k-Tx_k=2(-1)^ka\), so every pointwise residual has norm \(2|a|\). For every even \(N\), uniform averaging over \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\) gives \(\bar x_N=0\) and \(\bar r_N=0\). Thus a zero averaged residual does not imply that any sampled iterate has a small pointwise residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating iterates can have residuals that cancel perfectly in the average while every individual residual remains large.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is positive and even, with uniform averaging.

notation.meaning: uniform average of the first N residual vectors

knowledge_statements.title: Black-Box Operator-Evaluation Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic oracle model for an otherwise unknown fixed-point operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal T\) be a class of maps \(T:D\to X\). In the deterministic black-box operator-evaluation model, an algorithm selects \(x_0\in D\) independently of \(T\), receives \(y_k=Tx_k\), and for \(k\geq1\) selects \(x_k\) as a deterministic function of \((x_0,y_0,\ldots,x_{k-1},y_{k-1})\). After \(q\) oracle calls it outputs a deterministic function of the same transcript. Its evaluation complexity for tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is the least \(q\) guaranteeing the prescribed residual certificate for every \(T\in\mathcal T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm learns an unknown operator only through adaptive point evaluations, and complexity counts evaluations needed for a uniform residual guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T\) is a specified class of single-valued maps \(T:D\to X\).
The oracle returns the exact value \(Tx_k\) at each queried point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle cost is the number \(q\) of evaluations, and a worst-case guarantee must hold for every \(T\in\mathcal T\).

knowledge_statements.title: Mann Iteration Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic scalar-relaxation model for fixed-point oracle evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a mapping \(T:C\to C\), an initial point \(x_0\in C\), and relaxation parameters \(\lambda_k\in[0,1]\), the Mann iteration queries \(T(x_k)\) and updates
\[
x_{k+1}=(1-\lambda_k)x_k+\lambda_kT(x_k),\qquad k\geq 0.
\]
The parameters may be fixed in advance or selected from the information available before the update. After \(N\) evaluations, the model outputs an iterate \(x_j\) with \(0\leq j\leq N\), or a prespecified function of the recorded iterates and residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each new iterate is a scalar convex average of the current point and its operator image, using only information available from previous oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty convex subset of a real normed space.

notation.meaning: Fixed-point operator queried by the method.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Hull Iteration Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle model allowing arbitrary convex recombination of previously revealed points and images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a mapping \(T:C\to C\) and initial point \(x_0\in C\), define the information set after queries at \(x_0,\ldots,x_k\) by
\[
\mathcal I_k=\{x_0,
egthinspace\ldots,
egthinspace x_k,T(x_0),
egthinspace\ldots,
egthinspace T(x_k)\}.
\]
A convex-hull iteration model requires
\[
x_{k+1}\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal I_k).
\]
Equivalently, the next query is a convex combination of the revealed points and operator values, with coefficients measurable with respect to the accumulated deterministic information. The model does not permit extrapolative coefficients whose sum of absolute negative parts is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The next query may be any convex combination of all points and operator values revealed so far, but it may not extrapolate outside their convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty convex subset of a real vector space.

notation.meaning: Information revealed through the k-th operator query.
Convex hull of a set S.

children.title: Averaging-Class Separation
children.top_down_role: Expressiveness gaps among restricted averaging classes used in sharp comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Averaging-Class Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural inclusion and conditional strict separation of Mann and history-convex update classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Every Mann trajectory is admissible in the convex-hull model: induction gives \(x_k\in\operatorname{conv}\{x_0,T(x_0),\ldots,T(x_{k-1})\}\), and the Mann update is a convex combination of \(x_k\) and \(T(x_k)\). For a fixed revealed history, let
\[
M_k=[x_k,T(x_k)],\qquad H_k=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal I_k).
\]
Then \(M_k\subseteq H_k\). If \(H_k\) contains a point outside the segment \(M_k\), the inclusion is strict, so a convex-hull method can select a next query that no Mann update from the same current state and history can select.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mann updates form a subclass of history-convex updates; the inclusion is strict whenever the revealed convex hull is larger than the current update segment.
assumptions_latex: The two models use the same mapping, initial point, and revealed history.

notation.meaning: Set of next points allowed by a Mann update.
Set of next points allowed by the convex-hull model.

children.title: Linear-Subspace Information Model Hierarchy

children.title: Span-Restricted Models
children.top_down_role: Models limiting iterates to linear spans of previously available information.

knowledge_statements.title: Span-Restricted Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-oracle model restricting queries to affine spans of previously observed residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:X\to X\), choose \(x_0\in X\), and write \(g_i=x_i-T(x_i)\). A deterministic residual-oracle method is span restricted when its queries satisfy
\[
x_k\in x_0+\operatorname{span}\{g_0,
egthinspace\ldots,
egthinspace g_{k-1}\},\qquad k\geq1.
\]
Thus there exist coefficients \(a_{k,0},\ldots,a_{k,k-1}\in\mathbb R\), chosen from the previously revealed information, such that \(x_k=x_0+\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}a_{k,i}g_i\). The model permits negative coefficients and therefore differs from a convex-hull information model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each query differs from the initial point by a linear combination of residual vectors obtained at earlier queries; extrapolative coefficients are allowed.
assumptions_latex: Each query reveals the exact value \(T(x_i)\).
review_flags: A source is needed to fix whether the intended model spans residuals, oracle images, or both.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A source is required to determine whether this hierarchy restricts spans of residuals, oracle images, or both, and to establish the associated information conventions.

children.title: Krylov-Restricted Models
children.top_down_role: Affine fixed-point models governed by Krylov information spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov-Restricted Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine fixed-point model whose query displacements belong to residual Krylov spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T(x)=Ax+b\) on a finite-dimensional real vector space and define \(B=I-A\) and \(g_0=x_0-T(x_0)\). The order-\(k\) residual Krylov space is
\[
\mathcal K_k(B,g_0)=\operatorname{span}\{g_0,Bg_0,
egthinspace\ldots,
egthinspace B^{k-1}g_0\}.
\]
A method is Krylov restricted when
\[
x_k\in x_0+\mathcal K_k(B,g_0),\qquad k\geq1.
\]
Equivalently, \(x_k=x_0+q_{k-1}(B)g_0\) for some real polynomial \(q_{k-1}\) of degree at most \(k-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine map, the k-th query displacement must lie in the Krylov space generated by the initial residual and the linear residual operator.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is finite dimensional over \(\mathbb R\).
The oracle returns exact operator values.

notation.meaning: Linear part of the residual mapping.
Order-k Krylov space generated by B and g_0.

review_flags: A source is needed to confirm whether the hierarchy uses Krylov spaces of A, I-A, or an equivalent residual operator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-Krylov formulation is internally consistent, but a source must confirm that the terminal uses the Krylov space generated by I-A rather than A or another equivalent operator convention.

children.title: Span-to-Krylov Specialization
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which a general span restriction reduces to Krylov structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Span-to-Krylov Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine specialization of residual-span trajectories to residual Krylov subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(T(x)=Ax+b\), set \(B=I-A\), and let \(g_i=x_i-T(x_i)\). Then
\[
g_i=g_0+B(x_i-x_0).
\]
If a trajectory is span restricted, induction on \(k\) yields \(x_i-x_0\in\mathcal K_i(B,g_0)\) and hence \(g_i\in\mathcal K_{i+1}(B,g_0)\). Consequently,
\[
x_k-x_0\in\operatorname{span}\{g_0,
egthinspace\ldots,
egthinspace g_{k-1}\}\subseteq\mathcal K_k(B,g_0).
\]
Thus every residual-span-restricted trajectory for an affine map is Krylov restricted, although a particular trajectory need not generate the entire Krylov space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For affine maps, every residual-span query lies in the corresponding residual Krylov space; the generated residual span may be a proper subspace.

notation.meaning: Residual Krylov space of order k.

children.title: Stochastic Operator-Oracle Model
children.top_down_role: Complexity under noisy samples, minibatches, and variance control.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Operator-Oracle Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased noisy operator evaluations with bounded conditional variance and minibatch averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A stochastic operator oracle queried at \(x_k\) returns \(G(x_k,\xi_{k,j})\) for samples \(1\leq j\leq b_k\). Relative to the pre-query information \(\mathcal F_k\), it satisfies
\[
\mathbb E[G(x_k,\xi_{k,j})\mid\mathcal F_k]=T(x_k),\qquad
\mathbb E[\|G(x_k,\xi_{k,j})-T(x_k)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq\sigma^2.
\]
For conditionally independent samples, the minibatch estimate \(\widehat T_k=b_k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{b_k}G(x_k,\xi_{k,j})\) is conditionally unbiased and has conditional mean-square error at most \(\sigma^2/b_k\). An algorithm may choose \(x_k\) and \(b_k\) using \(\mathcal F_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each query returns an unbiased noisy operator value. Averaging b conditionally independent samples preserves unbiasedness and reduces the conditional variance bound by a factor of b.
assumptions_latex: Oracle samples within each minibatch are conditionally independent given \(\mathcal F_k\).
The displayed conditional second-moment bound holds uniformly over queried points.
The ambient norm is induced by an inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\widehat T_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=T(x_k)\) and \(\mathbb E[\|\widehat T_k-T(x_k)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq\sigma^2/b_k\).

notation.meaning: Information available before the k-th query.

children.title: Nonexpansive-Map Residual Bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Nonexpansive-Map Residual Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-iterate residual guarantee for constant-relaxation Krasnoselʹskiĭ–Mann iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive with a fixed point, choose \(\lambda\in(0,1)\), and set \(x_{i+1}=(1-\lambda)x_i+\lambda T(x_i)\). For every \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}(T)\) and integer \(N\geq1\),
\[
\lambda(1-\lambda)\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\|x_i-T(x_i)\|^2\leq\|x_0-z\|^2.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\min_{0\leq i<N}\|x_i-T(x_i)\|\leq
\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x_0,\operatorname{Fix}(T))}{\sqrt{N\lambda(1-\lambda)}}.
\]
Thus an iterate with residual at most \(\varepsilon\) is guaranteed within \(N=O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) exact operator evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constant-relaxation fixed-point iteration on a nonexpansive map achieves a best-iterate residual of order one over the square root of the number of evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space.

notation.meaning: Set of fixed points of T.

children.title: Affine-Map Residual Bounds
children.top_down_role: Sharper guarantees enabled by affine structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Map Residual Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial residual characterization for affine maps under Krylov-restricted minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T(x)=Ax+b\), define \(B=I-A\), and let \(g(x)=x-T(x)=Bx-b\). Every Krylov-restricted point \(x_k=x_0+q_{k-1}(B)g_0\) has residual
\[
g(x_k)=p_k(B)g_0,
\]
where \(p_k(t)=1+tq_{k-1}(t)\), \(\deg p_k\leq k\), and \(p_k(0)=1\). Hence a method choosing the minimum-residual point in \(x_0+\mathcal K_k(B,g_0)\) satisfies
\[
\|g(x_k)\|=
\min_{\substack{p\in\mathbb R[t]\,:
\deg p\leq k,\ p(0)=1}}
\|p(B)g_0\|.
\]
Any uniform polynomial approximation bound on the relevant spectrum or numerical range therefore gives an affine-map residual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For affine maps, a Krylov method's residual is a polynomial of the residual operator applied to the initial residual; minimum residual equals the best admissible polynomial value.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is finite dimensional and Euclidean.
The k-th point minimizes residual norm over \(x_0+\mathcal K_k(B,g_0)\).

notation.meaning: Residual polynomial of degree at most k.

review_flags: A source is required for the exact polynomial residual bound and its intended spectral or numerical-range specialization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial residual characterization is plausible, but no source supports the exact Krylov minimum-residual identity or its intended spectral specialization. As written, it is primarily a representation rather than a concrete complexity bound.

children.title: Regularity-Sensitive Residual Bounds

children.title: Contractive Residual Bounds
children.top_down_role: Residual guarantees driven by strict contraction geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractive Residual Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric residual decay for Picard iteration of a strict contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:C\to C\) be a contraction with modulus \(q\in[0,1)\), and generate Picard iterates \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\). Then \(T\) has a unique fixed point \(x_\star\), and for every \(k\geq0\),
\[
\|x_k-T(x_k)\|=\|T^kx_0-T^{k+1}x_0\|
\leq q^k\|x_0-T(x_0)\|.
\]
Also,
\[
\|x_k-T(x_k)\|\leq(1+q)q^k\|x_0-x_\star\|.
\]
Thus residual accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\) follows after \(k\geq\log(\|x_0-T(x_0)\|/\varepsilon)/\log(1/q)\) iterations when \(q\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Picard iteration of a q-contraction reduces the fixed-point residual geometrically by at least a factor q per exact operator evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed subset of a complete metric linear space.

children.title: Conditioned Residual Bounds
children.top_down_role: Residual guarantees driven by error bounds, metric subregularity, or related conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioned Residual Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear convergence induced by an averaged operator and a global residual error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:C\to C\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged and suppose the residual error bound
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{Fix}(T))\leq\kappa\|x-T(x)\|
\]
holds for all Picard iterates. With \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\), averagedness gives
\[
d_{k+1}^2\leq d_k^2-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\|x_k-T(x_k)\|^2,
\]
where \(d_k=\operatorname{dist}(x_k,\operatorname{Fix}(T))\). Therefore
\[
d_k\leq\rho^k d_0,
\qquad
\rho=\sqrt{1-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha\kappa^2}}<1,
\]
and nonexpansiveness yields \(\|x_k-T(x_k)\|\leq2\rho^k d_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An averaged map with a residual error bound has geometrically decreasing distance to its fixed-point set and a corresponding geometric residual upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space and \(\operatorname{Fix}(T)\neq\varnothing\).
The residual error bound holds along the Picard trajectory, with \((1-\alpha)/(\alpha\kappa^2)<1\).

notation.meaning: Distance from x_k to the fixed-point set.

review_flags: A source is needed for the precise global or trajectory-local error-bound hypothesis and the stated linear factor.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed rate follows under the stated averagedness and trajectory error-bound assumptions, but a source is required for the exact conditioning convention, locality of the error bound, and contraction factor used by this hierarchy.

children.title: Contraction-to-Conditioning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Overlap and separation between contraction-based and regularity-based guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Contraction-to-Conditioning Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation of contraction modulus into residual conditioning and comparison of resulting rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(T:C\to C\) is a contraction with modulus \(q<1\) and fixed point \(x_\star\), then for every \(x\in C\),
\[
(1-q)\|x-x_\star\|
\leq\|x-T(x)\|
\leq(1+q)\|x-x_\star\|.
\]
Hence contraction implies the residual error bound
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{Fix}(T))\leq\frac{1}{1-q}\|x-T(x)\|,
\]
so the induced conditioning constant is \(\kappa=(1-q)^{-1}\). As \(q\uparrow1\), this constant diverges and generic conditioning-based estimates deteriorate; when the contraction modulus is known, the direct Picard residual factor \(q^k\) remains the sharper structural guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A q-contraction has residual conditioning constant at most one over one minus q; conditioning degenerates as q approaches one, while direct contraction analysis retains factor q.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is complete and \(T:C\to C\) is a contraction with modulus \(0\leq q<1\).
\(x_\star\) denotes the unique fixed point of \(T\).

children.title: Stochastic Residual Bounds
children.top_down_role: Residual guarantees under stochastic operator evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Residual Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected squared residual bound for stochastic Krasnosel'skii–Mann iteration with mini-batched unbiased operator estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive, and let \(x_\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\). For \(R=I-T\), consider \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\lambda_k\widehat R_k(x_k)\), where \(0<\lambda_k<1\), \(\mathbb E[\widehat R_k(x_k)\mid x_k]=R(x_k)\), and \(\mathbb E[\|\widehat R_k(x_k)-R(x_k)\|^2\mid x_k]\le \sigma^2/b_k\). Then
\[\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\lambda_k(1-\lambda_k)\mathbb E\|R(x_k)\|^2\le \|x_0-x_\star\|^2+\sigma^2\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\frac{\lambda_k^2}{b_k}.\]
Consequently, a random index \(K\) drawn proportionally to \(\lambda_k(1-\lambda_k)\) satisfies the corresponding right-hand side divided by \(\sum_k\lambda_k(1-\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The expected residual is controlled by the initial distance plus accumulated mini-batch variance, divided by the total effective relaxation weight.
assumptions_latex: The residual oracle is conditionally unbiased with variance at most \(\sigma^2/b_k\).

children.title: Stochastic Sample-Complexity Bounds
children.top_down_role: Oracle-sample requirements for attaining certified residual levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Sample-Complexity Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle complexity obtained from constant relaxation and explicitly chosen constant mini-batching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stochastic residual model, suppose \(\|x_0-x_\star\|\le D\), take \(\lambda_k=1/2\), and use a constant batch size \(b\). If \(K\) is uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,N-1\}\), then
\[\mathbb E\|R(x_K)\|^2\le \frac{4D^2}{N}+\frac{\sigma^2}{b}.\]
For \(\varepsilon>0\), choose
\[N=\max\{1,\lceil 8D^2/\varepsilon^2\rceil\},\qquad b=\max\{1,\lceil 2\sigma^2/\varepsilon^2\rceil\}.\]
Then \(\mathbb E\|R(x_K)\|^2\le\varepsilon^2\), and the number of individual stochastic operator samples satisfies
\[Nb\le \left(1+\frac{8D^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right)\left(1+\frac{2\sigma^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right).\]
In the regime where both leading terms dominate, this is \(O(D^2\sigma^2\varepsilon^{-4})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With explicit integer choices, constant mini-batching attains root-mean-square residual epsilon using at most the displayed product of deterministic and stochastic complexity terms; its leading joint term is of order epsilon to the minus four.
assumptions_latex: The hypotheses of the stochastic residual bound hold.
Each batch of size \(b\) costs \(b\) individual oracle samples.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Sample Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit iteration–batch tradeoff for a prescribed expected residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With constant relaxation \(\lambda\in(0,1)\), constant batch size \(b\), and \(\|x_0-x_\star\|\le D\), the relaxation-weighted stochastic residual estimate becomes
\[\mathbb E\|R(x_K)\|^2\le \frac{D^2}{N\lambda(1-\lambda)}+\frac{\lambda\sigma^2}{(1-\lambda)b}.\]
Hence a pair \((N,b)\) is certified to attain root-mean-square residual at most \(\varepsilon\) whenever the displayed right-hand side is at most \(\varepsilon^2\). Increasing \(b\) lowers the noise floor but does not reduce the deterministic iteration term; increasing \(N\) has the complementary effect.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteration count controls the deterministic residual term, while batch size controls the stochastic noise floor.
assumptions_latex: The stochastic residual-bound hypotheses hold with constant \(\lambda\) and \(b\).

children.title: Inexact-Operator Residual Bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Operator Residual Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic transfer from an observable approximate residual to the true fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:H\to H\) be an operator and let \(\widetilde T_k:H\to H\) satisfy \(\|\widetilde T_kx-Tx\|\le\delta_k\) at the evaluated point \(x\). Define the true and observed residuals by \(r(x)=\|x-Tx\|\) and \(\widetilde r_k(x)=\|x-\widetilde T_kx\|\). The triangle inequality gives
\[|r(x)-\widetilde r_k(x)|\le\delta_k.\]
Therefore \(r(x)\le\widetilde r_k(x)+\delta_k\), and an observed stopping test \(\widetilde r_k(x)\le\varepsilon-\delta_k\), with \(\delta_k\le\varepsilon\), certifies the true residual bound \(r(x)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate operator residual differs from the true residual by no more than the deterministic operator-evaluation error.

children.title: General Operator-Query Lower Bounds

knowledge_statements.title: General Operator-Query Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-unrestricted deterministic black-box lower bound for nonexpansive fixed-point residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider deterministic algorithms that make at most \(N\) adaptive value queries to an unknown nonexpansive map \(T:H\to H\), where the Hilbert-space dimension may depend on \(N\), and then output a point determined by the transcript. For a universal constant \(c>0\), the worst-case class containing maps with some \(x_\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) and \(\|x_0-x_\star\|\le D\) satisfies
\[\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_T\|x_{\mathcal A,N}-T(x_{\mathcal A,N})\|\ge \frac{cD}{N+1}.\]
Thus no general deterministic operator-query method guarantees residual at most \(\varepsilon\) with fewer than order \(D/\varepsilon\) queries in this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any deterministic black-box method needs order D over epsilon operator queries in the worst case for nonexpansive fixed-point residuals.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm receives only adaptive exact value queries to \(T\).
The adversary may choose a Hilbert-space dimension depending on \(N\).
A fixed point lies within distance \(D\) of the prescribed initial point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N=\Omega(D/\varepsilon)\) queries are necessary for a uniform guarantee \(\|x-Tx\|\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: initial distance bound to a fixed point

children.title: Mann-Iteration Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Barriers specific to convex-combination iteration families.

knowledge_statements.title: Mann-Iteration Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-sharp lower bound for constant-relaxation Mann iterations, witnessed by planar rotations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and apply \(x_{k+1}=(1-\alpha)x_k+\alpha T x_k\). For every \(N\) satisfying \(4\alpha(1-\alpha)(N+1)\ge1\), there is a planar linear isometry \(T\) with fixed point \(0\) and an initial point \(\|x_0\|=D\) such that
\[\|x_N-Tx_N\|=\frac{D}{\sqrt{\alpha(1-\alpha)(N+1)}}\left(\frac{N}{N+1}\right)^{N/2}.\]
Consequently, the worst-case residual of constant-relaxation Mann iteration is at least a universal constant times \(D/\sqrt{\alpha(1-\alpha)N}\); an order faster than \(N^{-1/2}\) is impossible for this iteration family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A suitably chosen planar rotation forces constant-relaxation Mann iteration to have residual of order one over square root N.
assumptions_latex: The operator class includes planar linear isometries.

notation.meaning: initial distance to the fixed point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula is algebraically plausible and properly restricted to constant-relaxation Mann iteration, but the exact lower-bound claim and its worst-case interpretation require an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Stochastic Fixed-Point Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Sample-complexity barriers under noisy operator access.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Fixed-Point Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax sample lower bounds under unbiased noisy operator access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an oracle return \(Y(x)\) with \(\mathbb E[Y(x)]=T(x)\) and \(\mathbb E\|Y(x)-T(x)\|^2\le\sigma^2\). Over nonexpansive maps having a fixed point within distance \(D\) of \(x_0\), any method guaranteeing \(\mathbb E\|x-Tx\|^2\le\varepsilon^2\) uniformly must use
\[N=\Omega\left(\max\left\{\frac{D}{\varepsilon},\frac{\sigma^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right\}\right)\]
individual oracle samples. The first term follows from the noiseless subclass; the second is present already for one-dimensional constant maps \(T_\theta(x)=\theta\) observed with additive centered noise, where residual minimization contains mean estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy fixed-point computation inherits both deterministic query difficulty and the sigma-squared over epsilon-squared mean-estimation barrier.
assumptions_latex: Oracle samples are conditionally independent and unbiased with variance bounded by \(\sigma^2\).
The guarantee is uniform over the stated nonexpansive-map class.
The ambient dimension is unrestricted for the deterministic component.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic and mean-estimation barriers are plausible, but their combination requires a sourced minimax oracle model and applicable parameter or accuracy regimes. The deterministic component also depends on the unsourced general query lower bound.

children.title: Sharp Worst-Case Construction Family
children.top_down_role: Construction families used to certify sharp residual bounds.

children.title: Residual-Bound Tightness
children.top_down_role: Matching regimes used to assess whether residual guarantees are sharp.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Bound Tightness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and order-wise notions of worst-case tightness for residual upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an algorithm class \(\mathfrak A\), an operator class \(\mathfrak T\), an initialization class \(\mathfrak X\), and a horizon \(N\). For residual performance
\[W_N=\sup_{(T,x_0)\in\mathfrak T\times\mathfrak X}\|x_N-Tx_N\|,\]
an upper bound \(W_N\le U_N\) is exact if \(W_N=U_N\). It is order-tight if there exists a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(N\) and the accuracy parameter, and admissible instances for which \(\|x_N-Tx_N\|\ge cU_N\). Tightness must use the same oracle model, operator class, initialization constraints, output rule, and residual norm as the upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual upper bound is tight when admissible instances match it exactly or up to a horizon-independent constant under the same model.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm, operator, initialization, output, and residual conventions are fixed.
\(U_N\) is a valid uniform upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact tightness means \(W_N=U_N\); order tightness means \(W_N\ge cU_N\) for a uniform \(c>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct content kind, but the formula fixes an algorithm class while using an unspecified single sequence x_N. A performance-estimation reference and clarification of whether the algorithm is fixed or optimized over are required.

children.title: Worst-Case Instance Constructions
children.top_down_role: Adversarial instance families supporting fixed-point complexity lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Instance Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A horizon-dependent rotation family witnessing slow Mann residual decay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and horizon \(N\) with \(4\alpha(1-\alpha)(N+1)\ge1\), set
\[\sin^2(\theta_N/2)=\frac{1}{4\alpha(1-\alpha)(N+1)}.\]
On \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(T_N\) be rotation through \(\theta_N\), choose \(\|x_0\|=D\), and run \(x_{k+1}=(1-\alpha)x_k+\alpha T_Nx_k\). This admissible nonexpansive instance has fixed point \(0\) and satisfies
\[\|x_N-T_Nx_N\|=\frac{D}{\sqrt{\alpha(1-\alpha)(N+1)}}\left(\frac{N}{N+1}\right)^{N/2},\]
thereby furnishing an explicit worst-case lower-bound family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rotations whose angle depends on the horizon explicitly produce the square-root residual barrier for Mann iteration.
assumptions_latex: The admissible operator class contains nonexpansive planar rotations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rotation construction and residual formula are internally consistent and fit the construction leaf, but no source supports the exact formula or the characterization as a worst-case lower-bound family.

children.title: Extremal Operator Constructions
children.top_down_role: Operator families engineered to expose limiting residual behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Extremal Operator Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual formula for relaxed iteration of a planar isometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Identify \(\mathbb R^2\) with \(\mathbb C\), and define the isometry \(T_\theta z=e^{i\theta}z\). For constant \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the relaxed fixed-point iteration admits the exact representation
\[z_N=(1-\alpha+\alpha e^{i\theta})^Nz_0,\qquad \|z_N-T_\theta z_N\|=2\|z_0\||\sin(\theta/2)|\bigl(1-4\alpha(1-\alpha)\sin^2(\theta/2)\bigr)^{N/2}.\]
Thus optimizing the scalar angle \(\theta\) produces explicit extremal candidates for residual performance. In particular, the interior maximizer satisfies \(\sin^2(\theta/2)=1/[4\alpha(1-\alpha)(N+1)]\) whenever this value does not exceed one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Planar rotations reduce worst-case relaxed residual analysis to a one-variable maximization with an exact closed formula.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The planar-rotation representation is internally consistent, but an authoritative locator is missing. The source should also distinguish extremality within the rotation family from extremality over all admissible operators.

children.title: Performance Estimation for Fixed-Point Iterations
children.top_down_role: Performance-estimation mechanisms for parameter design and sharp analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Performance Estimation for Fixed-Point Iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Gram representation of worst-case residual analysis for nonexpansive maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For sampled pairs \((x_i,y_i)\) intended to satisfy \(y_i=Tx_i\), finite nonexpansive interpolation requires
\[\|y_i-y_j\|^2\le\|x_i-x_j\|^2\quad\text{for all }i,j.\]
Include a fixed-point pair \((x_\star,y_\star)\) with \(y_\star=x_\star\), impose the linear iteration relations defining each \(x_i\), and normalize the initial condition. Introducing the Gram matrix of all vectors appearing in these relations converts every squared norm and inner product into a linear matrix functional. Maximizing \(\|x_N-y_N\|^2\) subject to those linear constraints and positive semidefiniteness yields a semidefinite performance-estimation problem for the worst-case fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonexpansive interpolation and a Gram matrix turn worst-case residual analysis of fixed-step iterations into a semidefinite program.
assumptions_latex: Only finitely many iterates and operator images are modeled.
Iteration relations are affine in the stored vectors.
The ambient Hilbert-space dimension is unrestricted or sufficiently large.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Worst-case \(\|x_N-Tx_N\|^2\) is represented by a Gram-matrix semidefinite optimization problem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gram-matrix SDP representation fits the performance-estimation leaf, but finite nonexpansive interpolation and exact worst-case equivalence require a specific theorem or section citation and explicit dimension conditions.

children.title: Universal Residual Certification Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies for reaching certified residual levels without unavailable constants or horizons.

children.title: Residual-Based Stopping
children.top_down_role: Termination based on observable fixed-point certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Based Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable, conditional termination certificate for approximate fixed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a normed space, let \(T:H\to H\), define \(R=I-T\), and fix \(\varepsilon>0\). For exact operator evaluations, define
\[S=\{k\ge0:\|R(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\}.\]
If \(S\ne\varnothing\), terminate at \(\tau=\min S\) and output \(x_\tau\); then the computed residual certifies \(\|x_\tau-Tx_\tau\|\le\varepsilon\). If instead an approximation \(\widetilde T_kx_k\) is available with a certified bound \(\|\widetilde T_kx_k-Tx_k\|\le\delta_k\), where \(\delta_k\ge0\), use
\[S=\{k\ge0:\|x_k-\widetilde T_kx_k\|+\delta_k\le\varepsilon\}.\]
Whenever this set is nonempty, its first index likewise yields an output satisfying \(\|x_\tau-Tx_\tau\|\le\varepsilon\). No finite-termination claim is made when the applicable set \(S\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop at the first iterate whose exact residual, or whose approximate residual plus certified evaluation error, is at most the tolerance; if such an iterate exists, the returned point is certified.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a normed space and \(T:H\to H\).
The operator value or a certified inexact value is available at each tested iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the applicable certified-index set \(S\) is nonempty, the returned point satisfies \(\|x_\tau-Tx_\tau\|\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: set of indices passing the applicable certified residual test
first certified stopping index when S is nonempty
